learning_parts.title: Financial mathematics, statistics and numerical methods
learning_parts.introduction: Learn the mathematics behind every later Part: discounting, cash-flow valuation and return measurement; probability and statistical inference; regression and time-series econometrics; stochastic processes and calculus; Bayesian inference; high-dimensional covariance estimation; and the numerical methods used to price and optimise. Their use in financial research begins in Part [[part:empirical-finance-research-governance]].

learning_parts.title: Empirical finance, machine learning and research governance
learning_parts.introduction: Apply the methods of Part [[part:mathematics-statistics-numerics]] to test asset-pricing models, identify causal effects, build auditable research, meet professional and ethical duties, and evaluate machine-learning and alternative-data evidence. Keep three questions apart throughout: whether a variable predicts returns, whether a pricing model explains them, and whether an action caused an effect.

learning_parts.title: Public markets and pricing
learning_parts.introduction: Progress from rates and government bonds, through the financial statements and corporate finance of issuers, to credit, securitisation, equities and derivatives, and then to cross-asset, currency, international equity and regional market decisions.

learning_parts.title: Portfolio financing and execution
learning_parts.introduction: Build and evaluate portfolios, connect them to funding, collateral and liabilities, then study market microstructure and the cost of executing orders across asset classes.

learning_parts.title: Energy and commodities
learning_parts.introduction: Study storage, curves, hedging and options, then spot price formation, market integration and long-run prices, physical delivery, price discovery and trading, commodity risk premia, factor strategies and allocation, oil-price shocks, forecasting and their macro-financial effects, gas hubs and network-constrained power markets, and emissions trading, carbon credits and certificates.

learning_parts.title: Private capital, real assets and insurance
learning_parts.introduction: Evaluate long-dated contractual cash flows, asset rights and contingent claims, then apply public and private investments, insurance and conduct duties to a private client's wealth.

learning_parts.title: Digital assets
learning_parts.introduction: Apply earlier pricing, market-making and validation tools to digital-asset venues and derivatives, crypto spot markets, on-chain claims, fractional and tokenised assets, market making on centralised and decentralised venues, and crypto trading strategies. Event contracts, including on-chain prediction markets, are in Part [[part:event-contracts]].

learning_parts.title: Event contracts and prediction markets
learning_parts.introduction: Read, trade and supply liquidity to contracts that pay a fixed amount if an event happens: exchange-listed event contracts, on-chain prediction markets and bookmaker and exchange betting markets. Start with what a price reveals, then study venues, outcome tokens, resolution and regulation, and finally market making, event derivatives and trading strategies. No crypto background is assumed.

routes.name: Systematic equities
routes.outcome: Rebuild a stock characteristic from point-in-time inputs and judge whether its return survives weighting choices, the exclusion of microcaps, trading costs and the move from the original sample to post-publication and forward-only periods.

section_goals.goal: construct and time factor premia and measure their crash risk
design residual mean-reversion and pairs strategies
estimate demand elasticities, flow-driven price impact and the effects of passive ownership
turn financial statements into valuation and accounting signals
test short-selling, option, insider and retail-flow signals
combine signals into a neutral long--short portfolio with a matched risk model
measure event returns and size merger-arbitrage positions

routes.prerequisites: Asset pricing theory and empirical tests; equity returns, corporate actions, survivorship and basic factor regressions.

required_readings.reason: Start with the factor benchmark against which a proposed stock signal must be compared.
Study a canonical anomaly and the choices needed to turn a return spread into a portfolio.
Reconstruct definitions, reporting lags, breakpoints and weighting from reusable characteristic code.
Test how standardized constructions and microcap exposure reduce apparent anomaly evidence.
Compare a different replication design and global evidence before declaring a factor either real or refuted.
Move from gross return spreads to turnover-aware entry, hold and exit decisions.
Distinguish original-sample performance from later decay and crowding after disclosure.
Finish with a risk and trading-cost frontier; test desk-specific capacity, borrow and financing separately.

routes.checkpoint: Rebuild two stock characteristics from point-in-time inputs. Report equal- and value-weighted results with and without microcaps, then net returns under turnover, borrow and impact assumptions; record original, postpublication and forward-only periods separately.

optional_branches.reason: Add cash-flow valuation, ETF creation/redemption and transmission into underlying stocks.
Add filing and news signals after the factor benchmark is stable.
Study a modern conditional SDF architecture after replication and implementability.
Use a practical empirical asset-pricing manual.
Read how equity long--short, quantitative and event-driven managers trade and where their returns come from.

routes.learning_note: Start from factor premia, statistical arbitrage, investor flows and fundamental valuation; then study short-selling, option, insider and retail-flow signals, combine signals into a risk-controlled long–short portfolio, and finish with corporate events and merger arbitrage.

routes.name: Multi-asset and systematic macro
routes.outcome: Attribute a cross-asset portfolio's returns to carry, trend, value and rate exposures, using signals built from release vintages and tradable contract rolls, and show how funding haircuts, trading costs and a rapid unwind change the result.

section_goals.goal: build and judge value, momentum, carry and defensive premia across asset classes
construct and evaluate diversified trend-following strategies
build risk-parity and volatility-targeted portfolios and decide their leverage
measure asset-price responses and premia around macro announcements and policy news
identify macro regimes in real time and model the stock--bond correlation
build real-time nowcasts and macro trading signals without look-ahead

routes.prerequisites: Asset pricing theory and empirical tests; futures, bond duration and collateral mechanics. Currencies follow in the next section.

required_readings.reason: Learn the economic foundations (output, inflation, and monetary and fiscal policy) that macro signals and regimes assume.
Map expected returns to risk premia and the limits of historical cross-asset comparisons.
Set long-run base rates for equities, bonds, bills and currencies across countries before trusting a short sample.
Define carry consistently across assets before interpreting it as expected return.
Contrast trend exposure with carry and understand the path dependence of crisis behavior.
Build macro signals from release calendars and revisions, not final revised series.
Decompose a bond yield into expected short rates and estimated term premium.
Model the feedback between funding constraints and the liquidity available to unwind positions.
Translate forecasts into paced trades when signals decay and transaction costs matter.

routes.checkpoint: Build a dated cross-asset signal panel using release vintages and tradable contract rolls. Attribute one portfolio's returns to carry, trend, value and rate exposures, then rerun with funding haircuts, transaction costs and a rapid unwind.

optional_branches.reason: Explore systematic macro practice, books and history in more depth.
Deepen term-premium and bond-liquidity research.
Deepen a specific high-frequency, trend, factor or volatility-inference method after standard econometrics.
Revisit expected returns, factor premia and alternatives when markets offer little.
Read a 2026 practitioner text on trading macro regimes across rates, FX, equities and emerging markets.
Compare systematic rules with how discretionary macro managers frame trades.
Use reflexivity between beliefs, prices, policy and financing to frame stress scenarios.
Place current debt and crisis indicators in eight centuries of history.

routes.learning_note: Start with cross-asset style premia, trend following, risk parity and macro announcements; macro regimes and the stock–bond correlation build on risk parity, and nowcasting builds on announcements. Currencies follow in their own section.

routes.name: Currency markets: exchange rates, premia and hedging
routes.outcome: From spot, forward and money-market rates, measure forward-implied carry, covered-interest-parity deviations and realised currency excess returns, and show how a carry portfolio behaves in the worst equity months.

section_goals.goal: test exchange-rate forecasts and explain the forward-premium puzzle and the role of order flow
price FX forwards and options with market conventions, and follow fixes and settlement
build carry, momentum, value and dollar portfolios and judge their risk explanations
measure the cross-currency basis and price synthetic dollar funding
read currency risk-neutral distributions and separate crash, volatility and carry premia
choose a currency-hedge ratio for international portfolios
classify exchange-rate regimes, judge pegs and intervention, and stress emerging-market currency positions

routes.prerequisites: Multi-asset and systematic macro; money-market discounting and forwards.

required_readings.reason: Survey exchange-rate determination under uncovered interest parity and its failures.
Use dated instrument and currency turnover definitions.
Learn how the FX market is organised and who trades in it.
Sort currencies into portfolios and find their common risk factors.
Measure covered-interest-parity deviations after 2008.
Connect currency carry positions to monetary-policy transmission and unwind risk; treat policy analysis as contextual evidence.

routes.checkpoint: For five currencies against the dollar, assemble daily spot, one-month forwards and deposit or OIS rates. Compute forward-implied carry, covered-interest-parity deviations and realised excess returns, and compare a carry portfolio's drawdowns with the dollar's moves in the worst equity months.

optional_branches.reason: Browse the currency risk premia and factors section.
Model asymmetric dependence between exchange rates.
See the dollar's W-shaped return pattern around the FX fixes.
Survey currency risk and what it implies for interest rates, capital allocation and policy.
Work through a graduate text on exchange-rate theory and evidence.
Use a textbook treatment of parity conditions, currency risk management and international portfolios.

routes.learning_note: Start with exchange-rate determination and with FX forwards, options, fixes and settlement. Currency premia build on determination, and covered interest parity and dollar funding on the instruments; continue to FX volatility and crash risk, then currency hedging and emerging-market currencies and intervention, which draw on both premia and funding. FX dealing is in Part [[part:portfolio-financing-execution]].

routes.name: Rates: yield curves, term premia and derivatives
routes.outcome: Connect a rate quote or bond position to its curve, expected policy path, term premium, collateral and hedge-contract assumptions.

section_goals.goal: build zero curves and estimate and compare affine term-structure models
price caps, swaptions and SOFR futures with calibrated models and risk-free-rate conventions
read the expected policy path and separate policy, term-premium and balance-sheet channels
forecast bond excess returns and build systematic rates signals
price inflation-linked bonds and swaps and decompose breakevens

routes.prerequisites: Financial mathematics and return measurement; discount factors, bond cash flows, swaps and futures.

required_readings.reason: Frame the yield curve through expected policy, time-varying term premia and macroeconomic news.
Establish arbitrage-consistent term-structure modelling and rate-derivative notation.
Use an empirical decomposition to distinguish expected policy from estimated term premium.
Tie a modern overnight-rate curve and swap hedge to exchange-traded contract conventions.
Close the valuation loop with collateral, counterparty exposure, funding, margin and capital, using the July 2026 fifth edition.

routes.checkpoint: Build a cash-flow and risk-assumption sheet for one collateralised swap hedged with SOFR futures and one Treasury note. Reprice both under level and slope moves, a policy-path surprise, a term-premium shock and a collateral or funding change; identify assumptions that cannot all hold together.

optional_branches.reason: Extend the curve and cash-flow framework to inflation indexation.
Compare the retained historical third edition of the xVA text.

routes.learning_note: Build curves and rate-derivative conventions, then read monetary policy and term premia in the curve, forecast bond excess returns and price inflation-linked claims.

routes.name: Government bond markets and sovereign debt
routes.outcome: For a Treasury, a euro-area or UK government bond and an emerging-market local-currency bond, explain each bond's spread to swaps or to Treasuries from its issuance calendar, holders, dealer and repo capacity, central-bank backstop and credit or convertibility risk.

section_goals.goal: explain how dealer balance sheets, clearing and basis trades shape Treasury liquidity and stress
explain how auctions, issuance and investor demand set the supply and price of government debt
assess sovereign default, restructuring and local-currency risk
value municipal bonds from pledge, tax treatment, disclosure and trading costs
compare euro-area, UK and Japanese government bond markets, their backstops and stress episodes

routes.prerequisites: Rates: yield curves, term premia and derivatives; repo and money-market basics.

required_readings.reason: Survey how dealer intermediation, transparency and electronic trading shape fixed-income liquidity.
Read the case for redesigning Treasury market intermediation after March 2020.
Compare the convenience premium of Treasuries with other developed-market government bonds.
Set two centuries of sovereign bond returns, defaults and haircuts against the safe-asset benchmark.

routes.checkpoint: For one U.S. Treasury, one euro-area or UK government bond and one emerging-market local-currency bond, record at a dated decision point the issuance calendar, main holders, dealer and repo liquidity, central-bank backstop and credit or convertibility risk. Explain which of these drives each bond's spread to swaps or to Treasuries, and state which inputs need licensed data.

optional_branches.reason: Browse the sovereign and municipal debt catalogue section.
Browse the government debt issuance catalogue section.

routes.learning_note: Study Treasury market structure and issuance, sovereign default and restructuring, and municipal bonds; then compare euro-area, UK and Japanese markets with the Treasury market.

routes.name: Corporate credit, hybrids and labelled bonds
routes.outcome: Decompose a bank's senior bond, CDS and AT1 or Tier 2 spreads into expected loss, liquidity and contract features, and show which claim the capital structure protects first.

section_goals.goal: price default with structural and reduced-form models and aggregate portfolio losses
reconcile cash-bond spreads, CDS values and bond-return evidence
value AT1, CoCo and Tier 2 bank capital by coupon, conversion, call and resolution terms
value corporate hybrids and preferred shares by deferral, subordination and calls
separate use-of-proceeds claims, contingent coupons and pricing evidence in labelled bonds

routes.prerequisites: Rates: yield curves, term premia and derivatives, and Financial statement analysis for issuer accounts; hazard rates, recovery, seniority and basic option exercise.

required_readings.reason: Add default, recovery and credit-spread modelling without confusing spread with expected loss.
Use cohort default and loss tables to compare a quoted spread with realised credit losses.
Bring sparse trading and corporate-bond liquidity into credit valuation.
Follow seniority, distress, bankruptcy and recovery across the capital structure before valuing a subordinated or hybrid claim.
required_readings.selection: Distress prediction, bankruptcy process and creditor-recovery topics (topic selection; chapter numbering is not inferred).

routes.checkpoint: For one bank, take a senior unsecured bond, its CDS and one AT1 or Tier 2 bond. Decompose each spread into expected loss, liquidity and contract features. Shock default probability, recovery and the coupon-cancellation or write-down trigger; explain which claim the capital structure protects first.
routes.learning_note: Model default and recovery, reconcile bond spreads with CDS, then study subordinated bank and corporate hybrids and sustainability-labelled bonds.

routes.name: Securitised and structured credit
routes.outcome: Follow collateral cash flows through prepayment, default, servicing and the waterfall to each tranche, and identify where the originator, issuer or sponsor retains risk.

section_goals.goal: model covered bonds: dual recourse, cover pools and payment extension
trace sukuk ownership, recourse and default outcomes
model mortgage, ABS and CLO collateral and waterfalls
connect synthetic risk transfer to reference-pool losses and bank capital, and value tranches from a dependent pool-loss distribution under stated physical and risk-neutral assumptions
reconcile CMBS property cash flows, servicing advances and workouts

routes.prerequisites: Corporate credit, hybrids and labelled bonds; amortisation, prepayment options and legal seniority.

required_readings.reason: Treat mortgage prepayment as an endogenous cash-flow option rather than a fixed amortization schedule.
Trace a worked auto-ABS contract from collections through fees, note payments, reserves and residual cash; retain its single-programme limitation.
Add the origination-incentive layer: ease of securitisation changed screening and later default; keep its historical subprime threshold design in view.
Check whether securitisation moved risk off the sponsor once guarantees and capital treatment are traced.
Contrast an on-balance-sheet, dual-recourse covered bond with securitisation; the 2007 sample predates the EU covered-bond Directive.

routes.checkpoint: Build a monthly waterfall for one auto-ABS or RMBS deal from its offering terms. Shock prepayment speed, defaults, recoveries and servicer advances; report each tranche's cash flows and losses, then state who retains the first loss and how a covered bond on similar collateral would differ.

optional_branches.reason: Inspect actual RMBS, CMBS, ABS and CLO waterfalls and reporting.

routes.learning_note: Compare dual-recourse and asset-based structures, then model mortgage, ABS and CLO cash flows and synthetic risk transfer; CMBS builds on the mortgage, ABS and CLO waterfalls.

routes.name: Option pricing, volatility models and hedging
routes.outcome: Fit an arbitrage-free volatility surface to an option chain and compare delta and delta--vega hedges of one position on profit and loss, costs and tail losses under observed and stressed smile moves.

section_goals.goal: calibrate local, stochastic and jump models and compare their smile dynamics
value convertible bonds from default, equity optionality and stock borrow
compare rough, path-dependent and Markovian volatility models
choose and test hedges under smile dynamics and costs, and attribute option profit and loss
use learned pricers and deep solvers with model-risk bounds
price and hedge exotic options, autocallables and structured products

routes.prerequisites: Stochastic processes and calculus; elementary option payoffs and numerical programming.

required_readings.reason: Establish option payoffs, Greeks, hedging and market conventions before fitting a model.
Derive the replication argument whose failures (discrete rehedging, costs, jumps and the smile) organise the rest of the section.
See which option-price bounds and relations hold by no-arbitrage alone, before any distributional assumption.
Learn how observed smiles and skews constrain a usable implied-volatility surface.
Use no-arbitrage extreme-strike restrictions as a check on extrapolation.
Construct and test a surface for static arbitrage across strikes and maturities.
Price path-dependent exposure and quantify numerical error with Monte Carlo methods.

routes.checkpoint: Fit a small option chain across two expiries, show calendar and butterfly-arbitrage diagnostics, and hedge one position with delta and delta-vega rules. Compare P&L, costs and tail losses under observed and stressed smile moves.

optional_branches.reason: Read a rigorous treatment of martingale pricing, change of measure and incomplete markets.
Browse the catalogue section on convertibles, exotics and structured products.
Study Gaussian-process surrogates and uncertainty for pricing, curves or stopping problems.

routes.learning_note: Start with stochastic, local and jump models, or with convertibles, a separate entry point; then rough and path-dependent volatility and the hedges each model implies, learned pricing, and exotics and structured products. Volatility trading and option premia are in the next section; crypto options appear with digital assets.

routes.name: Volatility trading, option premia and implied information
routes.outcome: Measure the variance risk premium and risk-neutral volatility and skewness in index and single-stock options, and test how much of the premium survives crash months, quoted spreads and margin.

section_goals.goal: replicate variance claims, measure variance and skew premia, and trace dealer gamma hedging
extract risk-neutral densities, tail measures and jump premia and test what they forecast
explain single-stock option returns with volatility, characteristics and option factors
price and hedge VIX, correlation, dispersion and dividend claims
price short-dated options and measure what retail option traders pay

routes.prerequisites: Option pricing, volatility models and hedging; time-series volatility forecasting.

required_readings.reason: See how a practitioner forecasts volatility, judges implied against realised volatility and sizes option trades.
Distinguish priced variance exposure from a model's volatility forecast.
Compute model-free risk-neutral volatility, skewness and kurtosis from a strip of options.
Weigh why index puts have earned such negative returns and which explanations fall short.
Price index option portfolios with a crisis factor before calling put returns an anomaly.
See that selling insurance-like payoffs earns a premium across markets, with crash losses as its cost.
Map variance swaps, dispersion, skew and term-structure trades to the exposures they carry.

routes.checkpoint: For SPX and five liquid single stocks, compute each month the at-the-money implied volatility, model-free implied variance and risk-neutral skewness, then the next month's realised variance and the delta-hedged return of a short at-the-money straddle. Report the average variance premium, its losses in crash months and how much of it survives quoted spreads and margin.

optional_branches.reason: Browse the catalogue section on variance, correlation, VIX and dividend claims.
Browse the catalogue section on option-implied densities, recovery and tail risk.

routes.learning_note: Start with index option returns, variance premia and dealer hedging and with option-implied densities and tail risk; continue to single-stock option returns, VIX, correlation and dividend claims, and short-dated and retail option trading. Options market making is in Part [[part:portfolio-financing-execution]].

routes.name: Market microstructure and market making
routes.outcome: Evaluate a quoting policy on an order-book replay by fill probability, adverse selection and inventory risk, and state how the result depends on queue-position and self-impact assumptions.

section_goals.goal: derive inventory-aware quotes and model queues and fill probabilities
train order-book prediction models with leakage-free evaluation
explain option spreads and the routing and cost of retail option orders
quote bonds and swaps on request within dealer balance-sheet limits
build and validate market simulators
price an FX client franchise, choose between internalising and hedging, and judge last look
evaluate high-frequency trading, latency races and market design

routes.prerequisites: Stochastic processes and calculus; limit orders, order-book events and elementary stochastic processes.

required_readings.reason: Start from order types, trading motives and who bears the cost of immediacy.
Turn trades and quotes into empirical measures of liquidity and price discovery.
Use inventory-sensitive quotes and stylised fill intensities as a market-making benchmark, then test their assumptions.
Model placement across venues with uncertain fills and explicit order costs.
Make queue state and event arrival part of the simulation rather than assuming every touched quote fills.
Test whether a simulator reproduces relevant market responses before using it to rank policies.

routes.checkpoint: Replay one order-book day with order acknowledgements, cancellations, fills and missed fills. Compare a passive limit order with an inventory-limited quote policy using fill probability, adverse selection and inventory risk, and test how the result depends on queue-position and self-impact assumptions.

optional_branches.reason: Extend replay into counterfactual and generative market simulation.

routes.learning_note: Study order-book mechanics and market making, then order-book learning, options market making, dealer market making in bonds and swaps, and simulation; FX dealing builds on bond and swap dealing, and high-frequency trading is a separate entry point. Crypto venues apply the same tools in Part [[part:digital-assets]].

routes.name: Execution, trading costs and market structure
routes.outcome: Plan the execution of an equity order, a futures roll and a bond trade, estimate expected cost and its uncertainty from a stated impact model, and split realised implementation shortfall into spread, impact, timing and fees under the rules in force.

section_goals.goal: estimate price impact, derive optimal schedules and measure implementation shortfall
track how U.S. and EU market-structure rules change execution quality
measure what clients pay in bond, swap and FX dealer markets
trade around ETF creations, index events and closing auctions
execute futures orders and rolls under each contract's matching and settlement rules
judge how retail CFDs are priced, margined and regulated

routes.prerequisites: Market microstructure and market making; stochastic control basics for optimal execution.

required_readings.reason: Define implementation shortfall as the gap between paper and realised portfolio returns.
Set a benchmark for the trade-off between impact risk and execution speed.
Calibrate costs from a large live-trading sample before assuming a cost model.
Compare price impact in the closing auction, the opening auction and the continuous market.
See how dealer markets change what cost and liquidity mean.
Check how wholesale FX conventions and algorithmic execution alter venue and benchmark choices.

routes.checkpoint: For an equity order, a futures roll and a bond trade of similar notional, choose a venue, mechanism and schedule for each. Estimate expected cost and its uncertainty from a stated impact model, then measure implementation shortfall against arrival price, split into spread, impact, timing and fees under the tick, fee and reporting rules in force.

optional_branches.reason: Follow wholesale FX order, disclosure and settlement conventions.
Compare search and dealer-intermediation frictions across OTC gilt and corporate-bond markets.

routes.learning_note: Start with price impact and transaction-cost analysis, the rules that shape execution quality, and dealer-market bonds and FX; then execution around ETFs and index events and in futures, which build on price impact, and retail CFD markets, which build on the rules.

routes.name: Machine learning and alternative data
routes.outcome: Test whether a filing-text feature adds decision-time predictive value beyond a dictionary measure and a simple market baseline, reporting coverage, missingness, the full model search and loss uncertainty.

section_goals.goal: fit, tune and validate regularised, tree-based and neural models on dependent, non-stationary data
train machine-learning return models against economic restrictions and costs
evaluate machine-learning and language-model results with time-valid inputs, uncertainty and portfolio tests
benchmark deep and foundation forecasters and check generated scenarios before use
train reinforcement-learning policies and compare them with control-theoretic benchmarks
build time-valid text signals and evaluate language-model and agent strategies
value alternative datasets by coverage, timing and incremental information

routes.prerequisites: Regression and time-series econometrics; programming in Python or R. Reading the overview for orientation assumes no machine learning; the checkpoint uses supervised learning and time-aware validation from Statistical learning foundations and time-series validation ([[statistical-learning-foundations]]) and the evaluation protocol of Financial ML: information timing, uncertainty and portfolio tests ([[financial-ml-evaluation]]).

required_readings.reason: Define alternative-data sourcing, coverage and lawful use before modelling a signal.
Use a primary filing interface and record submission, acceptance and revision times.
Learn why financial language requires domain-specific text features and interpretation.
Set a finance-specific model benchmark against simpler text measures.
Treat nonrandom missingness and changing coverage as part of the research design.
Frame language-model outputs as measured variables subject to validity and leakage checks.
Control inference across the full recorded family of features and model variants.
Report uncertainty among close forecasting models instead of selecting one by minimum observed loss.

routes.checkpoint: Create a filing-text feature with a documented release-time join and coverage history. Compare a dictionary, finance-language model and simple market baseline on untouched chronological data; report missingness, the complete model search and loss uncertainty before any portfolio claim.

optional_branches.reason: Compare financial time-series models with broader forecasting benchmarks.
Use causal identification when the intended claim is an effect of information or an action.
Extend feature design to delayed institutional-holdings representations.
Study satellite data with clear information timing.
Build economic-link graph signals.

routes.learning_note: Start with statistical learning and time-series validation ([[statistical-learning-foundations]]): return prediction, financial-ML evaluation, deep forecasting and reinforcement learning build on it, and text and alternative data build on the evaluation pathway ([[financial-ml-evaluation]]). The overview checkpoint closes the section after Statistical learning foundations and time-series validation ([[statistical-learning-foundations]]) and Financial ML: information timing, uncertainty and portfolio tests ([[financial-ml-evaluation]]).

routes.name: Portfolio construction and risk
routes.outcome: Construct and evaluate a portfolio whose forecasts, risk model, constraints, costs and tail measures are explicit and testable.

section_goals.goal: construct constrained portfolios with factor risk models, shrinkage and costs
forecast and backtest VaR and expected shortfall, design tail hedges and run systemic stress tests
attribute returns and separate manager skill from luck
measure climate exposure and test carbon and green premia

routes.prerequisites: Asset pricing, high-dimensional statistics and numerical optimisation overviews; portfolio exposure, covariance estimation and basic optimisation.

required_readings.reason: Express exposure and risk in a consistent multi-asset portfolio language.
Relate forecasts, breadth, risk models and constraints in an active portfolio; treat the fundamental law as an approximation when signals and costs are correlated.
Measure tails and dependence without treating a fitted distribution as a stress guarantee.

routes.checkpoint: Build a long-only and a long-short portfolio from the same forecasts and risk model. Report ex-ante and realised risk, turnover, costs and the largest tail-loss contributors; rerun with a shrunk covariance estimate and explain which decisions changed.

optional_branches.reason: Use the computational portfolio text for formulation, constraints and numerical comparisons.
Examine recent high-dimensional estimation claims alongside the existing risk and cost foundations.

routes.learning_note: Turn forecasts into constrained portfolios, measure tail and systemic risk, then evaluate managers and climate exposure.

routes.name: Funding, collateral and liquidity
routes.outcome: Assess whether a portfolio can meet liabilities, margin and borrow needs while liquidity and correlations deteriorate together.

section_goals.goal: trace how margin, leverage and crowding turn small shocks into forced liquidations
price repo, securities lending and short-term funding
build exposure and valuation-adjustment chains from contract terms
compare institutional investors' objectives, liabilities, governance and investment constraints, and choose liability hedges that remain fundable under stress
price CFDs and total return swaps from financing, dividend, borrow and margin terms

routes.prerequisites: Portfolio construction and risk; cash-flow timing, collateral and basic securities lending.

required_readings.reason: Shift the objective from asset return to funded status and liability-relative surplus.
Explain how margin pressure can feed back into thinner market liquidity.
Add stock-borrow availability and fees to short-portfolio financing.
Translate leveraged liability hedges into collateral and operational liquidity requirements.
Compare internal risk constraints and precautionary cash demand with the finding of broadly stable average repo financing in the March 2020 Treasury stress.
Locate clearing, settlement and margin obligations in the wider infrastructure that transmits stress.

routes.checkpoint: Construct a 10-day cash and collateral ladder for a leveraged portfolio. Shock prices, correlations, repo haircuts, stock-borrow availability and withdrawal depth together; identify the first binding payment, available actions and residual liability exposure.

optional_branches.reason: Follow pension, insurer, endowment and sovereign liability cases.
Deepen securities-lending contracts and price formation.

routes.learning_note: Start with funding and crowding, money markets and secured financing, collateral risk and asset-liability management, then combine financing and collateral risk in CFDs and total return swaps.

routes.name: Commodity futures: storage, curves, hedging and options
routes.outcome: Read a commodity futures curve through the theory of storage: compute the interest-adjusted basis, implied convenience yield and roll return, split a futures position's return into spot and roll, and judge a calendar-spread hedge of physical inventory.

section_goals.goal: explain forward curves from inventories and convenience yield and estimate the storage model
fit factor, seasonal and jump models to futures curves
size and roll hedges of physical exposure
price commodity, spread and swing options and value real options

routes.prerequisites: Financial mathematics and return measurement; forwards and futures, inventory accounting and basic constrained optimisation.

required_readings.reason: Ground spot and futures prices in production, inventories and physical scarcity.
Connect storage economics to the shape and dynamics of forward curves.
Test storage theory against a risk-premium reading of the basis across 21 commodities before choosing a pathway.
Get one framework for storage, forward curves and derivatives across agricultural, metal and energy markets before specialising.
required_readings.selection: Chapters on commodity markets, storage and forward curves; the metals and agriculture chapters support [[metals-storage-delivery]] and [[agricultural-futures-delivery]].

routes.checkpoint: Choose one storable commodity and download its futures curve on two dates, one in contango and one in backwardation. Compute the interest-adjusted basis, implied convenience yield and annualised roll return on each date, split a one-year futures position's return into spot and roll, and show how a calendar-spread hedge of a physical inventory performs between the two dates.

optional_branches.reason: Solve structural storage models numerically before the specialist pathways.

routes.learning_note: Start with the theory of storage. Term-structure models build on it and lead to options and real options; hedging also builds on storage theory. Spot price formation, market integration and long-run prices follow in the next section, then physical delivery, price discovery, individual markets and trading firms.

routes.name: Commodity spot markets: price formation, market integration and long-run prices
routes.outcome: For one commodity, explain who publishes its spot price and how that price compares with the nearby futures settlement, split its deflated long-run series into trend, cycle and short-run components, and name the policy interventions that moved it.

section_goals.goal: judge how spot benchmarks are assessed and when a contract should reference one
test spatial market integration and explain location differentials
date commodity cycles and tie their common factor to macro drivers
evaluate public stocks, price bands and export restrictions
test long-run price hypotheses and separate secular trends from supercycles

routes.prerequisites: Commodity futures: storage, curves, hedging and options, for the theory of storage and the basis: many spot prices are quoted as a basis or differential to a futures or forward price, so the futures foundations come first. Theory of storage, convenience yield and inventories ([[commodity-storage-curves]]) comes before the spatial-arbitrage pathway.

required_readings.reason: Survey the primary commodity universe: where commodities are produced and traded, how their prices are formed and trend, and the roles of exchanges, cartels, state ownership and depletion.
required_readings.selection: The chapters on the geography of commodity production and trade, price formation and price trends, commodity booms, and commodity exchanges, investments and speculation.

required_readings.reason: Compare the 1974 and 2008 commodity booms: simultaneous supply and demand surprises with low inventories, amplified by macro shocks and policy.
Read current spot-price levels, forecasts and risks across 46 commodities after the 2026 Strait of Hormuz disruption.
required_readings.selection: Executive summary and the chapter on your commodity group.

routes.checkpoint: Choose one commodity with a published spot assessment, a futures contract and at least fifty years of annual prices. State who publishes the spot price, from what data and at what time, and compare it with the nearby futures settlement over one volatile month. Deflate the long series by a manufactures price index and split it into trend, cycle and short-run components, and name the policy interventions---stock releases, export restrictions or price bands---that moved it.

optional_branches.reason: Add freight when transport costs set the spread between spot markets.

routes.learning_note: Spot price assessment, spatial arbitrage and price cycles are separate entry points. Price stabilisation and trade policy build on spatial arbitrage; long-run prices build on price cycles. Physical delivery, price discovery, individual markets and trading firms follow in the next section and use these benchmarks and location spreads.

routes.name: Physical commodity markets: delivery, price discovery and trading
routes.outcome: Specify a physically delivered contract's delivery terms and show how a delivery-rule change, a fundamental-data surprise and higher initial margin would each alter a calendar-spread hedge of a physical position.

section_goals.goal: read delivery terms and recognise convergence failures and manipulation
connect metal forward curves to inventories, delivery and lease economics
turn crop supply and use into a deliverable futures exposure
map crude and refined-product exposures to benchmarks and spreads
locate price discovery and measure reactions to fundamental reports
hedge freight with Baltic routes and freight forward agreements
follow trading-firm finance and margin stress through clearing and bank funding

routes.prerequisites: Commodity futures: storage, curves, hedging and options; commodity spot markets ([[commodity-spot-markets]]) helps for benchmarks and location spreads; exchange microstructure from Execution, trading costs and market structure helps but is not required.

required_readings.reason: See how physical traders transform commodities in space, time and form and manage the price and credit risk that futures hedge.
Ask why futures markets exist and why most new contracts fail before studying how delivery rules work.
Check how quality and delivery rules create a distinct agricultural basis.
required_readings.selection: ICE Coffee C futures rules; the paired USDA market report supplies optional physical-market context.

required_readings.reason: See how OTC exposure, margin calls and exchange intervention interacted in the March 2022 nickel squeeze before relying on delivery and clearing rules.

routes.checkpoint: Choose one physically delivered commodity contract and specify its delivery instrument, grades, locations, storage or shipping costs, and last trading and notice dates. Show how a delivery-rule change, a surprise in the weekly inventory or monthly crop report, and a doubling of initial margin would each alter a calendar-spread hedge of a physical position.

optional_branches.reason: Extend to freight and weather indices when logistics or climate is the binding risk.

routes.learning_note: Start with contract design and delivery: metals, agriculture and crude oil build on it. Price discovery and fundamental data, freight, and trading firms and margin stress are separate entry points; freight and trading firms also need hedging ([[commodity-hedging]]). Risk premia and commodity investing follow in the next section, and oil-price shocks in the one after.

routes.name: Commodity risk premia and investing: factors, allocation and index products
routes.outcome: Decompose commodity futures returns into spot and roll, measure their correlation with stocks, bonds and inflation by decade, and compare a long-only index, a long--short carry portfolio and an allocation to each inside a stock--bond portfolio.

section_goals.goal: separate spot, roll and risk premia and test hedging-pressure theories
build and test carry, momentum, trend, curve and skewness strategies
weigh the evidence on financialisation and speculation
size a strategic allocation for diversification and inflation hedging
read index methodologies and estimate roll and flow costs

routes.prerequisites: Commodity futures: storage, curves, hedging and options; carry and momentum across asset classes from Multi-asset and systematic macro; portfolio construction; time-series econometrics.

required_readings.reason: Start with the long-run evidence that collateralised commodity futures earned an equity-like premium with low correlation to stocks and bonds.
Separate roll return, spot return and diversification return before extrapolating that premium.
Survey what drives commodity futures returns and the debate over commodity investing.
See how financial investors changed risk sharing and information in commodity markets.

routes.checkpoint: For about two dozen liquid commodity futures since 1990, compute excess, spot and roll returns per commodity and for an equal-weight index. Report the index's correlation with equities, bonds and inflation by decade, and compare a long-only index, a long--short carry portfolio and a 10 per cent allocation to each inside a 60/40 stock--bond portfolio.

optional_branches.reason: See why managed-futures fund returns fall short of gross futures returns.
Set commodity returns against forty years of oil-price episodes, studied in the next section.

routes.learning_note: Start with the risk premia in commodity futures ([[commodity-premia]]). Factor strategies ([[commodity-factor-strategies]]), the financialisation evidence ([[commodity-financialisation]]) and strategic allocation ([[commodity-allocation-inflation]]) build on them, and index and ETF implementation ([[commodity-index-products]]) follows allocation. Oil-price shocks, forecasting and their macroeconomic and asset-price effects follow in the next section, then gas and power markets and environmental markets.

routes.name: Oil-price shocks, forecasting and the macroeconomy
routes.outcome: Decompose an oil-price spike into supply and demand shocks, compare no-change, futures and official forecasts made before it with the outcome, and estimate its effect on inflation and inflation expectations.

section_goals.goal: identify oil supply and demand shocks with structural VARs
build and evaluate real-time forecasts of the real price of oil
trace oil shocks into output, inflation and monetary policy
explain how oil shocks move equities, oil risk factors and currencies

routes.prerequisites: Commodity futures: storage, curves, hedging and options; time-series econometrics and structural VARs; commodity risk premia ([[commodity-investing-premia]]) for futures-based forecasts.

required_readings.reason: Start with the history of oil shocks from Suez to 2008 and the downturns that followed them.
Review forty years of oil-price episodes and why forecasts keep missing them.
Survey what energy-price shocks are, how they reach output, inflation and stock prices, and why demand and supply shocks must be separated.

routes.checkpoint: Take the oil-price spike of March 2026. Using monthly data since 1974, decompose it into supply, aggregate-demand and oil-specific demand shocks; compare the no-change and futures forecasts made in February 2026 with the EIA outlook of the same month and with the outcome; and estimate how much the spike added to US headline inflation and household inflation expectations.

optional_branches.reason: Survey the causes and consequences of oil-price shocks.
Read the World Bank's account of the 2026 Middle East supply shock and its price forecasts.

routes.learning_note: Start with structural identification ([[oil-price-shocks]]): forecasting ([[oil-price-forecasting]]), the macroeconomic transmission of oil shocks ([[oil-shocks-inflation-policy]]) and their effects on asset prices ([[oil-asset-prices]]) all use the shocks it identifies. Forecasting also uses the futures risk premia of Commodity risk premia: hedging pressure, inventories and the basis ([[commodity-premia]]). Gas and power markets follow in the next section, then environmental markets.

routes.name: Gas and power markets: hubs, storage, networks and market design
routes.outcome: Value a storage or dispatch asset's cash flows in a normal and a network-constrained week, and show how a data-release lag or a delivery-rule change alters its hedge.

section_goals.goal: test gas-market integration and oil indexation, and analyse supply shocks
value gas storage, transport and LNG options
explain nodal prices, congestion, PPA and storage cash flows
judge electricity market designs, capacity payments and market power
measure renewable value and price PPA risks
model and forecast electricity prices
trade intraday and balancing markets and value storage arbitrage

routes.prerequisites: Commodity futures: storage, curves, hedging and options; constrained optimisation and time-series forecasting.

required_readings.reason: Value the operating option in a capacity-constrained storage asset.
Use dated public inventory data while preserving release times and revisions.
See why nonstorability and load risk change electricity forward pricing.
Map power value to location, dispatch and ancillary-service market rules.
Test how probabilistic load and renewable forecasts improve day-ahead price forecasts; a profitable hedge needs a separate evaluation.

routes.checkpoint: Choose one storage or dispatch asset and specify location, capacity, losses, delivery windows and hedge contracts. Calculate cash flows across a normal and constrained week, then show how a data-release lag or delivery-rule change alters the hedge.

optional_branches.reason: Browse gas hub pricing, market integration and supply-shock studies.

routes.learning_note: Start with gas hub pricing and market integration ([[gas-hub-pricing]]), then value storage, transport and LNG options ([[physical-lng]]). Power networks and transmission rights ([[power-ftr]]) come before market design ([[power-market-design]]), renewable value ([[renewables-ppa-value]]), price modelling and forecasting ([[power-price-forecasting]]) and short-term markets and flexibility ([[power-short-term-flexibility]]). Environmental markets follow in the next section.

routes.name: Environmental markets: emissions trading, carbon credits and certificates
routes.outcome: For a compliance allowance, a voluntary credit and a fuel or electricity certificate, record the issuing authority, unit, eligibility and vintage rules, banking, price controls, registry and compliance deadline, and say which can be hedged with listed futures and what basis risk remains.

section_goals.goal: explain cap-and-trade design and the EU ETS supply rules
model allowance prices and hedge with allowance derivatives
measure cost pass-through and leakage and evaluate border carbon adjustment
judge the integrity and pricing of voluntary carbon and biodiversity credits
distinguish and price RECs, RINs and LCFS credits

routes.prerequisites: Commodity futures: storage, curves, hedging and options; futures pricing and intertemporal optimisation. Gas and power markets ([[power-gas-environmental]]) helps for fuel switching and cost pass-through.

required_readings.reason: Take stock of carbon markets after Kyoto and the shift to separate linked systems.
Compare carbon taxes, pure cap and trade and hybrids with price collars.
Compare emissions trading systems worldwide on coverage, caps and prices.

routes.checkpoint: Choose one compliance market (EU ETS, UK ETS, California--Quebec or RGGI), one voluntary-credit type and one tradable fuel or electricity certificate. For each, record the issuing authority, unit, eligibility and vintage rules, banking and borrowing, price controls, registry and compliance deadline, then say which can be hedged with listed futures and which basis risks remain.

optional_branches.reason: Separate allowance compliance, credit quality and physical-energy exposure.
Track carbon pricing instruments and revenues worldwide.

routes.learning_note: Start with cap-and-trade design ([[carbon-compliance-markets]]). Allowance prices and derivatives ([[carbon-allowance-derivatives]]), cost pass-through and leakage ([[carbon-pass-through-leakage]]), voluntary carbon and biodiversity credits ([[voluntary-carbon-credits]]) and renewable certificates and fuel credits ([[environmental-instruments]]) all build on it.

routes.name: Crypto settlement, venues and derivatives
routes.outcome: Trace a crypto position from custody and collateral through venue fragmentation, funding, quoting and option margin to its settlement risk.

section_goals.goal: trace stablecoin and tokenised-bond claims, reserves and redemption
reconcile spot, perpetual and dated-futures basis across venues
explain stablecoin pegs and stress the channels of a run
price and hedge linear and inverse crypto options in their settlement units
map crypto leverage and model liquidation cascades
build bitcoin volatility surfaces and decompose option premia

routes.prerequisites: Financial mathematics and return measurement; basic exchange microstructure, wallet transactions and futures or option payoffs.

required_readings.reason: Establish consensus, transactions and custody before analysing a token-market strategy.
Survey consensus, mining, stablecoins, DeFi and regulation as economic mechanisms before choosing a venue or protocol pathway.
Examine cross-venue crypto arbitrage with the transfer and settlement frictions that constrain it.

routes.checkpoint: For one perpetual future and one dated option on the same token, draw the path from deposited collateral to liquidation or settlement. Record the index, funding, margin and settlement-currency rules; compute the cross-venue basis net of transfer, funding and withdrawal frictions, then identify which leg fails first if a stablecoin used as collateral trades below par.

optional_branches.reason: Add stablecoin reserves, redemption and tokenised-claim settlement.
Use the current published syllabus as an introductory roadmap; the next advertised cohort begins in February 2027.
Use the transaction-programming selections to trace UTXOs, fees and settlement before exchange-transfer research.
Study the economic limits of Nakamoto consensus.
Read the original white paper for the settlement and issuance assumptions that later venue and custody rules rely on.
Use the public lecture slides for a rigorous course on consensus, Ethereum, DeFi and scaling.

routes.learning_note: Begin with custody, settlement and stablecoin collateral, then progress through cross-venue basis and crypto options. Three later pathways deepen each strand: stablecoin pegs and runs, leverage and liquidation cascades, and option-market evidence. Spot price discovery, exchange market quality, valuation, investors and exchange regulation follow in Section [[crypto-spot-markets]]; order-book dealing and other market making are in Section [[crypto-market-making]].

routes.name: On-chain protocols
routes.outcome: Trace an AMM swap and a collateralised loan from signed transaction to finality, attributing fees, loss-versus-rebalancing, transaction-ordering exposure and liquidation risk to the oracle, block builder or contract behind each.

section_goals.goal: price AMM swaps and routes and decompose liquidity-provider returns
measure who extracts value from transaction ordering
value staking, liquid-staking and restaking claims
model lending-pool liquidations and stress their oracles
price solver and cross-domain execution
classify contract, exploit, bridge and governance risk
separate causal crypto signals from factor exposure and data artefacts

routes.prerequisites: Crypto settlement, venues and derivatives; smart-contract transactions, probability and basic market microstructure.

required_readings.reason: Learn what smart contracts can and cannot enforce, and why oracles and legal enforcement remain outside them, before studying any protocol.
Map DeFi protocols by layer and function before studying any single mechanism.
Identify transaction ordering and MEV as execution and mechanism risks.
Compare price efficiency and trading costs on centralised and decentralised venues, including the gas fees that separate them.
Measure automated-market-maker losses relative to rebalancing and distinguish them from fee income.
Classify attacks by protocol layer so each exposure has a named failure mode before live use.
Translate each mechanism into the responsible persons, conflicts, risks and disclosures a securities regulator would look for.

routes.checkpoint: For one token swap through an AMM and one collateralised loan on a lending protocol, draw the complete path from signed transaction to finality. Attribute fees, loss-versus-rebalancing, transaction-ordering exposure and liquidation risk, and name the oracle, block-builder or contract dependency behind each exposure.

optional_branches.reason: Use the layered DeFi framework as a short first map.
Follow the BIS stack model through exchanges, lending, derivatives and aggregators, and see how composability creates systemic links.
Read a monograph-length treatment of exchange, lending, governance tokens and five classes of operational risk.
Compare a Federal Reserve staff overview of DeFi products and their stability risks.
Read the empirical survey of DEXs, lending, governance, liquidations and composability.
Use a book-length introduction to DeFi exchanges, lending, derivatives and tokenisation.
Follow the lecture series on AMMs, lending, MEV and security.
Inspect contract permissions and failure modes before live protocol exposure.
Use the transaction, token and EVM selections to reconstruct swaps; the companion docs are owned by this same entry.

routes.learning_note: Automated market makers, transaction ordering, staking, protocol risk and on-chain signals are separate entry points. Lending, liquidations and oracles build on AMMs; solver execution builds on both AMMs and transaction ordering. Tokenised securities traded in permissioned AMM pools are covered in Section [[tokenised-fractional-assets]].

routes.name: Event contracts and prediction markets
routes.outcome: Read an event-contract price as evidence only after accounting for contract wording, trader beliefs and wealth, fees, liquidity and the settlement path, and keep forecasting, decision and trading uses apart.

section_goals.goal: measure the calibration of event prices and use them in event studies
derive when an event price equals the mean belief
explain the favourite--longshot bias across market structures
design markets whose prices inform decisions

routes.prerequisites: Probability and statistical inference; probability, binary option payoffs and basic market microstructure. No crypto background is assumed; on-chain venues add their own settlement mechanics.

required_readings.reason: Build the baseline: contract types, information aggregation and the record on forecast accuracy.
Challenge the shortcut that a binary-contract price equals the average trader belief.
Read the reply: the conditions under which prices track mean beliefs, and where the gap remains.
Survey the evidence on speed, efficiency and accuracy, and how event prices can test economic models.
Treat event contracts as short-lived assets with a known terminal value, and meet the anomalies betting markets have shown for decades.

routes.checkpoint: Choose one resolved event contract. From its rulebook, write down the exact payoff, resolution source and settlement timing. Convert the last traded price into an implied probability, then list each adjustment needed before calling it a forecast: fees and spread, the favourite–longshot pattern, belief dispersion and trader wealth, and capital locked until payout. Compare it with one external forecast and score both after resolution with a proper scoring rule.

optional_branches.reason: Browse the full event-contract literature by theme, from price interpretation to venues, integrity and trading.
Choose a proper scoring rule before comparing event prices with other forecasts.
Read the 2008 case for legal, small-stakes prediction markets made by 22 economists.

routes.learning_note: Begin with what an event price can and cannot reveal. The four pathways are independent: the forecast record, the theory of prices under heterogeneous beliefs and wealth, the wagering-market evidence on bookmakers, exchanges and the favourite–longshot bias, and markets used to make decisions. Venues, settlement and regulation follow in Section [[event-contract-venues]]; market making, derivatives and strategies in Section [[event-contract-trading]].

routes.name: Event-contract venues, settlement and regulation
routes.outcome: Before using a price or volume series, state who lists the contract and under what licence, how a position is held and redeemed, who determines the outcome and how it can be disputed, and what the trade record may hide.

section_goals.goal: interpret prices only after resolution, dispute, payout and cash-release terms are explicit
represent event claims as tokens or exchange positions and match listings across venues
screen trade records for insider trading, manipulation and wash trading
state which authority governs a contract and what pending cases could change

routes.prerequisites: Event contracts and prediction markets ([[event-contracts-prediction-markets]]); binary-option payoffs and basic market microstructure. Tokenised and fractional assets ([[tokenised-fractional-assets]]) helps with on-chain venues but is not required.

required_readings.reason: Map the current venues, contract categories and open regulatory questions.
See how an exchange entered a market of bookmakers and came to coexist with them.
Learn how an on-chain position is minted, merged, converted and redeemed as fractional, collateralised tokens.
Compare an exchange's settlement and cash-release rules.
Read how an on-chain venue resolves markets through an optimistic oracle, and why the rules, not the title, define the payoff.
See why an on-chain event market was still a derivatives venue under U.S. law.

routes.checkpoint: Pick one event listed on a regulated exchange and on an on-chain venue. For each, record the legal wrapper, the position (contract, token identifier, fractional size and tick), the resolution source and dispute route, the settlement and cash-release timing, and the fees. List every way the two contracts could pay differently on the same real-world outcome, and say which price you would treat as the forecast.

optional_branches.reason: Track the 2026 CFTC event-contract proposal and the split over sports contracts.
Measure how often the same event is listed on several venues and how far prices diverge.

routes.learning_note: Four independent pathways: resolution and settlement data; outcome tokens, fractional contracts and cross-venue identity; insider trading, manipulation and wash trading; and regulation and litigation. Read the settlement pathway before using any realised-return data.

routes.name: Event-contract trading: market making, derivatives and strategies
routes.outcome: Measure maker and taker returns after fees by price level at one venue, size a stake with the Kelly rule, and decide whether to supply or take liquidity at that venue's fees.

section_goals.goal: design automated market makers and scoring rules for event contracts
quote event-contract order books and measure adverse selection
price event derivatives and model the volatility of a probability
test event-contract strategies net of fees and size them

routes.prerequisites: Event contracts and prediction markets ([[event-contracts-prediction-markets]]) and Event-contract venues, settlement and regulation ([[event-contract-venues]]); Market microstructure and market making for the order-book pathway.

required_readings.reason: Measure returns by price level and by maker or taker side on a regulated exchange.
See who wins on an on-chain venue: limit-order traders, not liquidity takers.
Apply a p(1 - p) fee schedule and see why it costs longshot buyers most per dollar.
Place event contracts in the derivatives toolkit.
Size a bet on an edge by growth of capital, not expected profit.

routes.checkpoint: Take one resolved market with full trade data. Compute the taker's return after fees by price bucket, the maker's return including any rebate, and the Kelly stake a trader with a stated edge would have chosen at the quoted price. State whether, at this venue's fees, the edge needed to justify taking liquidity is larger than the one needed to quote.

optional_branches.reason: Check the favourite–longshot bias on a large on-chain venue.

routes.learning_note: Four independent pathways: scoring-rule and automated market makers; order-book and request-for-quote market making; derivatives built on event prices (binary options, parimutuel auctions, combos and belief volatility); and trading strategies, arbitrage and stake sizing.

routes.name: Research engineering, data provenance and model validation
routes.outcome: Specify a strategy as a research record (decision timestamp, data vintages, candidate family, economic hypothesis and the evidence that would reject it) and reconstruct a research decision and its eventual trade from versioned identities, data events, experiments and control records.

section_goals.goal: report backtests with multiplicity-adjusted significance and Sharpe-ratio uncertainty
build research panels whose every field was available at decision time
design model inventories, validation and pre-trade controls
package research so that it rebuilds from raw inputs and can be monitored in production

routes.prerequisites: Probability and statistical inference, for uncertainty and resampling; database joins, event logs, version control and basic trading lifecycle terms.

required_readings.reason: Record the full family of strategies tried before treating the selected configuration as evidence, and estimate the probability that the selection is overfit.
Start with durable entity identities and delta updates rather than matching display names.
Test how a dataset format change alters security history and return construction.
Represent economic terms and lifecycle events as explicit trade-state transitions.
Connect submitted orders, acknowledgments, fills and cancels to protocol-level evidence.
Retain both effective and known-at times through corrections and restatements.
Reason about logs, consistency and replay failure in data-intensive systems.
Track code, inputs, parameters and model artifacts for each experiment.
Check whether risk data remain complete, timely and reconcilable across institutional systems.

routes.checkpoint: Write a one-page research record for a simple public-data signal: the decision timestamp, data vintages, candidate family, economic hypothesis, estimation window, the uncertainty of the headline estimate, risk limits and the evidence that would reject it. Then take one signal decision through raw source, normalised identity, historical revision, model run, order and final position, and produce a replay package that reproduces the decision and P&L after a corrected input arrives, including the failed run and reconciliation differences.

optional_branches.reason: Deepen model-risk, clearing and settlement controls.
Add replayable market scenarios for execution evaluation.
Adopt simple reproducibility rules.
Apply good-enough computing practices.

routes.learning_note: Specify the research object first; then make data availability, research records, code and trading events auditable and reproducible before assessing model evidence.

routes.name: Private equity, private credit and fund structures
routes.outcome: Measure a fund's performance from dated investor cash flows against a public benchmark, and show when delayed exits, extra calls, NAV financing or lower appraisals force an allocator to sell liquid assets or cut new commitments.

section_goals.goal: measure private-fund performance with PME, direct alpha and cash-flow returns
connect private-equity and venture security terms to fund performance
underwrite direct loans by covenant, collateral and restructuring waterfall
model trade-finance and purchased-receivables risk
value music and pharmaceutical royalty interests
underwrite litigation-finance cash flows
model capital calls, NAV leverage and redemptions in fund vehicles

routes.prerequisites: Financial mathematics and return measurement, and Corporate finance; discounting, fund cash flows, debt seniority and public-market benchmarks.

required_readings.reason: Introduce fund cash-flow performance, persistence and the need for a suitable vintage comparison.
Decompose the economics of management fees, carry and fund-level incentives.
Compare private-equity results with public-market alternatives using investor cash flows.
Risk-adjust private-debt fund returns instead of treating contractual yield as net alpha.
Recognise how appraisal smoothing distorts measured volatility and cross-asset comparisons.
Model the cyclicality of calls and distributions that drives allocator liquidity.
Examine how NAV financing changes liquidity, leverage, governance and reported timing.
Use a reporting template to request comparable gross, net and cash-flow evidence.

routes.checkpoint: Build a quarterly LP cash-flow ledger for a fund and a public benchmark. Calculate a net cash-flow comparison, then stress delayed exits, extra calls, a NAV facility and lower appraisal values; show when the allocator must sell liquid assets or cut new commitments.

optional_branches.reason: Move from allocation to transaction and security underwriting.
Deepen commitment pacing, subscription lines and continuation vehicles.

routes.learning_note: Study ownership and credit claims, expand to other contractual cash flows, then evaluate fund liquidity.

routes.name: Real estate, infrastructure and natural-resource investments
routes.outcome: Underwrite contracted, regulated, biological and merchant cash flows with their distinct operating and refinancing risks.

section_goals.goal: reconcile property values with private indices and listed REIT returns
price contracted and regulated infrastructure cash flows
underwrite equipment and aircraft leases
value timber, farmland, mineral and water rights
evaluate collectibles from transaction evidence

routes.prerequisites: Financial mathematics and return measurement; discounted cash flows, debt service, property income and basic commodity forwards.

required_readings.reason: Establish property-level valuation, leasing cash flows and real-estate financing.
required_readings.selection: Print chapter 4 (discounted cash flow) and chapter 10 (leases), fourth edition (2026).

required_readings.reason: Check what an appraised property index measures and omits before benchmarking a deal.
Structure project cash flows, contracts and debt around construction and operation phases.
Trace concession obligations, construction handover, performance deductions and refinancing into valuation.
Compare infrastructure's reported investor outcomes with claims of stable, diversifying returns.
Value timber rotations and land use as biological and timing decisions.
Connect farmland prices to expected income and capitalization assumptions.
Add a physical operating option whose value depends on capacity and market spreads.

routes.checkpoint: Prepare a comparable cash-flow map for one property, one concession and one biological or storage asset. Identify contracted and merchant revenue, operating limits, debt and residual value; calculate how a demand shock and a refinancing shock change each equity value.

optional_branches.reason: Deepen farmland, timber and biological-asset measurement.
Extend to oil, gas, metals, crops and delivery-location options.

routes.learning_note: Begin with property and infrastructure valuation, then examine leased equipment, resource rights and collectibles.

routes.name: Insurance and climate-linked risk
routes.outcome: Distinguish insured-loss and weather-risk transfer from carbon compliance and credit retirement, preserving basis, model, collateral and reversal risks.

section_goals.goal: assess catastrophe and cyber bond cash flows
price longevity exposure
model station-level weather exposure and its basis
separate sidecar capital commitments, collateral release and distributions

routes.prerequisites: Probability and statistical inference; insurance layers, conditional loss distributions and basic derivative cash flows.

required_readings.reason: Examine limited purchases of high-layer catastrophe protection and the role of capital supply in pricing.
Distinguish annual occurrence and aggregate loss measures before using a catastrophe model.
Test how an index or parametric trigger can miss the insured's actual loss.
Build weather-index valuation from meteorological data and contract definitions.
Introduce stochastic mortality and parameter uncertainty for longevity exposure.
Model allowance banking and borrowing as policy-dependent intertemporal claims.
Assess voluntary-credit methodology and governance separately from allowance trading.
Use empirical over-crediting evidence to challenge additionality and claimed emissions reductions.

routes.checkpoint: For one catastrophe cover and one weather index, map exposure to payment and calculate a plausible basis-loss case. Separately compare one allowance with one project credit: record compliance or retirement purpose, additionality, reversal and settlement evidence without treating either as an insurance hedge.

optional_branches.reason: Inspect loss aggregation, sidecars and collateral-release evidence.
Compare allowance supply rules, exchange contracts and project-credit integrity.
See statutory capital frictions at life insurers.
Construct portfolios of insurable risks.

routes.learning_note: Build from insured loss and longevity claims toward weather payoffs and sidecar capital structures.

routes.name: Global and regional markets: capital flows, local bonds and market access
routes.outcome: Compare the hedged returns of two local-currency government bond markets from dated records of eligibility, tax, trading calendar, price source, custody, settlement, FX hedge terms and rule versions, marking every input that is unavailable.

section_goals.goal: separate push and pull drivers of capital flows and estimate benchmark-driven flow effects
decompose local-currency government bond yields and assess the risk from foreign holders
trace a local security through access, custody, settlement, tax, hedging and repatriation

routes.prerequisites: The Currency markets and Government bond markets overviews; settlement and macro data releases. The first pathway brings Emerging-market currencies, intervention and the global financial cycle ([[em-currencies-intervention]]), and the second Sovereign default, restructuring and local-currency debt ([[sovereign-municipal]]). International equity markets precede this section.

required_readings.reason: Start with a documented cross-country macro panel and its comparability limits.
Frame capital flows by push and pull drivers and by type of flow.
Separate local-currency sovereign credit risk from exchange-rate exposure.
Include cross-currency basis and funding when comparing hedged yields.
Use a concrete access channel to expose custody, trading and settlement conditions.
Treat FX permissions as dated, instrument-specific rules requiring the applicable circular and counterparties.
Compare country-level bond-market guides without inferring one ASEAN-wide access rule.
required_readings.selection: ADB bond-market guides for Indonesia and Thailand; the paired empirical foreign-flow paper is an optional extension.

required_readings.reason: Connect Brazilian local-rate contracts, clearing and nonresident participation.
Add an African-market route with an identifiable custody and settlement path.

routes.checkpoint: Choose two local-currency bond markets and build a dated, hedged-return comparison. Record instrument eligibility, tax, trading calendar, price source, custody, settlement cycle, FX hedge terms and rule version; mark every unavailable item before making a return claim.

optional_branches.reason: Follow country-specific empirical, instrument and access paths.
Deepen NDF, cross-currency funding and FX option conventions.
Add a Middle East local-debt path with sukuk and settlement detail.
Monitor EU securities-market risks in ESMA's risk monitor and statistical annex.

routes.learning_note: Start with capital flows and benchmark-driven investors, then local-currency government bonds, then trace a security through access, custody, settlement, tax and hedging. Equity integration, emerging-market equities and China are in the previous section.

routes.name: International and emerging equity markets
routes.outcome: Measure equity-market integration and diversification gains across developed, emerging and frontier markets without relying on raw correlations, in local currency and in dollars, hedged and unhedged, after survivorship, reclassification and stale-price corrections.

section_goals.goal: construct and maintain free-float-adjusted equity indices, price assets under integration and segmentation, measure integration and explain home bias
test factors and country-selection signals across countries
adapt equity research to emerging and frontier markets
trade cross-listed and asynchronously priced securities
adapt factor and machine-learning research to China's stock market and its access channels

routes.prerequisites: Systematic equities; currency translation and forward hedging from the Currency markets overview. Currency hedging for international portfolios ([[currency-hedging]]) helps.

required_readings.reason: Start with the survey of whether risk premia are set by world or local factors, and why holdings, flows and correlations defeat the simplest global models.
Use the 39-market record to see why US equity history is a survivor, not a base rate.
Organise the explanations of home bias: hedging motives, trade costs and information frictions.
Separate liberalisation from integration and survey what is distinctive about emerging-market finance.
Learn the institutions and research on China's stock market before applying US paradigms.

routes.checkpoint: Build a monthly panel of MSCI or FTSE country equity indices in local currency and US dollars from 1990, with each market's classification history. Compute rolling correlations, a factor-based integration measure and the diversification gain of an equal-weight portfolio, and report them separately for developed, emerging and frontier markets. Compare unhedged and currency-hedged returns, mark index inclusions and reclassifications, and state which conclusions survive survivorship and stale-price corrections.

optional_branches.reason: Put equity returns beside housing, bonds and bills for 16 countries since 1870.
Use long-run returns across many markets as base rates.
Use the harmonised global factor data for external-validity tests outside the US.

routes.learning_note: Start with integration, diversification and home bias. Global factors, emerging and frontier markets, and cross-listings build on it, and the China pathway draws on global factors and emerging-market evidence. Capital flows, local-currency bonds and market access follow in the next section.

routes.name: Crypto spot markets: price discovery, market quality, valuation and investors
routes.outcome: Reconstruct a crypto reference rate for one settlement window and compare it with venue, futures and spot-ETF prices, screen each venue's volume for wash trading, and identify which venues also custody client assets, trade for their own account or issue a token.
