section_goals.goal: measure where crypto prices are discovered and reconstruct reference rates
measure exchange liquidity, fake volume and manipulation
explain what equilibrium models say cryptocurrencies and tokens are worth
describe crypto investors, spot ETFs and bank custody rules
assess exchange counterparty risk and the rules for trading platforms
describe crypto return dynamics and test efficiency and bubbles

routes.prerequisites: Crypto settlement, venues and derivatives ([[digital-assets-prediction-markets]]), above all Makarov and Schoar on cross-exchange arbitrage; exchange order books and basic time-series econometrics.

required_readings.reason: Survey what drives cryptocurrency supply, demand, price and competition before choosing a pathway.
See where rents accumulate in crypto intermediation and why pseudonymous, permissionless design complicates enforcement.
Map the conflicts that arise when one platform lists, trades, custodies, lends and makes markets, and the recommendations regulators apply to them.
required_readings.selection: The executive summary and the list of eighteen recommendations; the 2025 thematic review's executive summary.

routes.checkpoint: Pick bitcoin or ether and one volatile trading day. From public trade data, recompute the CME CF reference rate for one settlement window from its constituent exchanges and compare it with each venue's last trade, the front CME future and one spot ETF's published NAV. Report each venue's volume before and after a wash-trading screen, and name which venues are multifunction intermediaries that also custody client assets, trade for their own account or issue a token.

optional_branches.reason: Use the catalogue section for the full spot-market literature, including entries not required here.
Read a 2020 practitioner view of fragmented, round-the-clock crypto market structure as historical context.

routes.learning_note: Price discovery, exchange market quality and valuation are separate entry points. Investors and spot ETFs build on price discovery; exchange failures and regulation build on market quality; return dynamics build on valuation. Derivatives on the same assets are in Section [[digital-assets-prediction-markets]]; on-chain trading and crypto return signals follow in Section [[onchain-protocols]].

routes.name: Fractional and tokenised assets: fractional shares, tokenised securities and real-world assets
routes.outcome: Explain what changes, and what does not, when ownership is cut into smaller units or recorded on a distributed ledger: the legal claim, the record of ownership, the trading venue and data, settlement, and the holder's recourse if an intermediary fails.

section_goals.goal: explain how fractional orders are executed and what odd lots do to market data
classify tokenised securities and funds and trace their settlement
compare token offerings and tokenised real assets with conventional finance

routes.prerequisites: Crypto settlement, venues and derivatives ([[digital-assets-prediction-markets]]) and Execution, trading costs and market structure ([[execution-trading-costs]]). On-chain protocols ([[onchain-protocols]]) helps for tokenised stocks traded in AMM pools.

required_readings.reason: See why share prices were held near a constant nominal level and why the trading unit is a design choice.
Define tokenisation and its claimed benefits, obstacles and vulnerabilities.
required_readings.selection: Executive summary and Sections 2--3.

required_readings.reason: Check where tokenisation has changed issuance, trading and settlement so far, and where it has not.
required_readings.selection: Executive summary and the life-cycle findings.

routes.checkpoint: Take one high-priced US stock held in three forms: a fractional position at a retail broker, a tokenised entitlement under the DTC pilot, and a third-party token on a crypto venue. For each, state the legal claim, the record of ownership, the custodian, the venue and trading hours, settlement, and the holder's position if the intermediary fails; then list what fractionalisation or tokenisation changed and what it left unchanged.

optional_branches.reason: Use the catalogue section for tokenised securities and real-world assets.
Use the catalogue subsection on fractional shares, odd lots and contract size.

routes.learning_note: Fractional shares and tokenised securities are separate entry points. Token offerings and tokenised real assets build on tokenised securities. Stablecoins, tokenised bonds and tokenised money market funds are in Stablecoins and tokenised bonds ([[stablecoin-tokenisation]]).

routes.name: Crypto market making: order books, DEX liquidity and token market makers
routes.outcome: Cost a day of two-sided liquidity on a centralised order book and in a concentrated-liquidity AMM pool, including fees, adverse selection, repositioning, inventory hedging and capital, and say which fills and costs could not be observed.

section_goals.goal: quote and hedge crypto inventory through order books and requests for quote
estimate fee, impact, latency and adverse-selection terms from a venue's data
read token market-making agreements and tell liquidity provision from manipulation
design and evaluate active AMM liquidity strategies
build and backtest model-based and learning market makers

routes.prerequisites: Market microstructure and market making ([[execution-market-making]]) and Crypto settlement, venues and derivatives ([[digital-assets-prediction-markets]]). On-chain protocols ([[onchain-protocols]]) for the DEX pathway, and Crypto exchange market quality ([[crypto-exchange-market-quality]]) for token market makers.

required_readings.reason: Learn the inventory, adverse-selection and execution models that every crypto quoting strategy adapts.
See how standard microstructure measures behave in crypto markets before quoting one.
Compare a limit order book and an AMM side by side, and how liquidity moves between them.
Measure trading costs and price efficiency on centralised and decentralised venues on the same assets.

routes.checkpoint: For one token pair traded on a centralised order book and in a Uniswap v3 pool, cost a day of USD 100,000 two-sided liquidity on each: maker fees or rebates, adverse selection from markouts, gas and repositioning for the LP, the cost of hedging inventory on a perpetual, and capital locked. State which quotes you could actually have been filled at, and which costs you could not observe.

optional_branches.reason: Start from the exchange-API and connector entries before collecting order-book data.

routes.learning_note: Order-book dealing and RFQ, order-book microstructure, token market makers and DEX liquidity provision are separate entry points; quoting strategies and learning agents build on order-book microstructure. AMM pricing and LP returns are in Section [[onchain-protocols]]; exchange market quality and wash trading are in Section [[crypto-spot-markets]]; perpetual hedging is in Section [[digital-assets-prediction-markets]].

routes.name: Crypto trading strategies: factors, trend, arbitrage, sentiment and machine learning
routes.outcome: Choose, test and size a crypto trading strategy other than market making, separating a persistent premium from a small-coin, high-cost or sample-specific artefact.

section_goals.goal: build cross-sectional crypto factor portfolios and manage their crash risk
test trend, intraday momentum and technical rules with data-snooping controls
build and test crypto statistical-arbitrage strategies
train and judge machine-learning crypto return forecasts
size cross-exchange, triangular, funding-basis and DeFi carry trades
test attention, sentiment and event signals

routes.prerequisites: Crypto spot markets ([[crypto-spot-markets]]); Empirical asset pricing: factor models and tests ([[empirical-asset-pricing]]); Backtest inference, multiple testing and Sharpe-ratio statistics ([[backtest-inference]]). Crypto perpetuals and cross-venue basis ([[crypto-perpetuals]]) for the carry pathway.

required_readings.reason: Start from the stylised facts of crypto as an asset class: comparable risk-adjusted returns, a few factors, frequent jumps and blockchain information.
Map the crypto trading literature by strategy family, data and evaluation before choosing one.
Use the market, size and momentum factors as the benchmark every strategy must beat.
Relate crypto returns to standard factors, momentum and investor attention.
Check how exchange coverage and provider choices change the price history a backtest uses.

routes.checkpoint: Pick one strategy from each of two families (for example short-term reversal and a funding-basis trade). For each, write the signal, universe filter, rebalancing rule, venues and cost model before looking at returns. Backtest both over the same period with point-in-time coin lists, delisted coins, exchange fees, spreads and borrow or funding, then report returns net of costs, capacity at realistic volume shares, exposure to the market, size and momentum factors, and the number of variants you tried.

optional_branches.reason: Add crypto to a multi-asset portfolio only in amounts that can actually be traded.
Compare mean--variance crypto portfolios with the 1/N benchmark out of sample.
Test common allocation models across coins against 1/N.
Test bitcoin in out-of-sample stock--bond portfolios.
Read practitioner evidence on digital assets in traditional allocations.

routes.learning_note: Cross-sectional factors, trend and technical rules, statistical arbitrage, arbitrage and carry, and sentiment and event strategies are separate entry points; machine-learning prediction builds on the cross-sectional pathway. Market making is in Section [[crypto-market-making]]; on-chain signals and wallet data are in Crypto signals and on-chain evidence ([[crypto-signals]]); option and volatility strategies are in Section [[digital-assets-prediction-markets]].

routes.name: Financial mathematics and return measurement
routes.outcome: Value a dated set of cash flows under stated compounding conventions, and compute the holding-period, time-weighted and money-weighted returns of a portfolio with external flows, explaining why they differ.

section_goals.goal: value cash-flow streams by discounting under stated compounding and quoting conventions, solve for internal rates of return and price a forward by cost of carry
measure simple, log, excess and total returns, link and annualise them, and compute time-weighted and money-weighted returns for portfolios with external flows

routes.prerequisites: Algebra, logarithms and exponentials, and calculation in a spreadsheet or Python. No finance background is assumed.

required_readings.reason: Learn compounding, discounting, annuities and interest-rate quoting from a free introductory text before any market convention.
required_readings.selection: Sections 3.4 (interest rates), 7.3--7.4 (time value of money) and 15.1 (risk and return of an individual asset).

required_readings.reason: See cash-flow valuation and interest-rate quoting in the corporate-finance setting that later sections reuse.
required_readings.selection: Part 2, Time, Money, and Interest Rates.

required_readings.reason: See how practitioners calculate and link portfolio returns before any risk adjustment or attribution.
required_readings.selection: Return-calculation chapters (topic selection).

routes.checkpoint: For a three-year coupon stream and a monthly-payment loan, compute present values under annual, monthly and continuous compounding and convert the quoted rates into one another. Then, for a fund with two external cash flows in one year, compute the holding-period, time-weighted and money-weighted returns and explain the gap between them.

optional_branches.reason: Browse the financial-mathematics and return-measurement references.
Continue to bond prices, yields and day counts, used throughout the rates sections.

routes.learning_note: Value cash flows before measuring returns: discounting, compounding conventions and internal rates of return come first, then holding-period, time-weighted and money-weighted returns.

routes.name: Probability and statistical inference
routes.outcome: Describe a return sample with appropriate summary statistics, state the distributional assumptions behind a test or interval, and say which assumption a financial series is most likely to violate.

section_goals.goal: derive the sampling distribution, test and asymptotic or bootstrap approximation behind an estimator, and state which assumptions each approximation needs
test tail and dependence assumptions and estimate extreme quantiles, expected shortfall and tail dependence

routes.prerequisites: Calculus and linear algebra; return definitions from Financial mathematics and return measurement ([[financial-mathematics]]).

required_readings.reason: Survey probability, estimation, testing and the bootstrap in one compact text before any specialist route.
Revise calculus-based probability, conditioning and the named distributions with problems and lectures.
Pair theory with data analysis: descriptive statistics, estimation and testing on real samples.

routes.checkpoint: For ten years of daily and monthly returns on an index and a single stock, report the mean, median, standard deviation, skewness, kurtosis, quantiles and first five autocorrelations with standard errors. Test normality and a zero mean, and for each test write one sentence naming the assumption (independence, identical distribution or finite moments) the data most likely violate.

optional_branches.reason: Deepen probability, inference or measure-theoretic prerequisites as needed.
Use the identified full-year graduate probability video and slide archive when a structured course is helpful.

routes.learning_note: Probability and statistical inference come first; heavy tails, extremes and dependence build on them. Regression, stochastic calculus and Bayesian methods in the following sections all assume this section.

routes.name: Regression and time-series econometrics
routes.outcome: Specify a regression or time-series model for a financial question, state which assumption delivers each reported standard error or test, and diagnose the failure most likely in the data.

section_goals.goal: estimate linear and multiple regressions, diagnose heteroskedasticity, serial correlation, misspecification and endogeneity, and estimate by instrumental variables and GMM
fit ARMA and VAR models, test for unit roots and estimate cointegration and error-correction models
build and evaluate volatility and regime models with proper loss functions, robust inference and break tests

routes.prerequisites: Probability and statistical inference; matrix algebra.

required_readings.reason: Connect financial time-series and cross-sectional evidence to the econometric assumptions behind it.
Frame forecasting and forecast evaluation as decisions under instability before fitting time-series models.

routes.checkpoint: Regress monthly excess returns of a portfolio on the market excess return and a lagged valuation ratio. Report OLS and HAC standard errors, residual diagnostics and a unit-root test on the valuation ratio, explain how a persistent regressor changes the interpretation of the slope, and name the assumption behind each reported p-value.

optional_branches.reason: Go further into multivariate VAR and cointegrated systems.

routes.learning_note: Regression comes first; stationarity, VARs and cointegration build on it, and volatility and regime models on both.

routes.name: Stochastic processes and calculus
routes.outcome: Explain Brownian motion, quadratic variation, the Itô integral, Itô's lemma and a change of measure well enough to derive the Black--Scholes PDE for a traded claim and to simulate the underlying SDE.

section_goals.goal: derive a hedging or allocation rule from an SDE model, state the dynamic-programming or BSDE problem it solves and simulate it with a convergent scheme

routes.prerequisites: Probability and statistical inference, including conditional expectation; ordinary differential equations.

required_readings.reason: Learn conditional expectation and martingales in the binomial model, then Brownian motion and Itô calculus.
required_readings.selection: Volume I (binomial model), then the opening chapters of Volume II on Brownian motion and stochastic calculus.

required_readings.reason: Learn SDEs, Itô's formula and their link to PDEs from an applied introduction.
See how change of measure, martingale pricing and the PDE approach fit together in continuous-time finance.

routes.checkpoint: Simulate Brownian motion and show that its quadratic variation over a fixed interval converges to the interval length while its total variation diverges as the grid is refined. Apply Itô's lemma to the logarithm of geometric Brownian motion, derive the Black--Scholes PDE by a replication argument, and check by Monte Carlo under the risk-neutral measure that the discounted stock price is a martingale.

optional_branches.reason: Browse the stochastic-processes references.

routes.learning_note: Brownian motion and Itô calculus precede SDEs, changes of measure and continuous-time control; the numerical pricing methods later in this Part use them.

routes.name: Bayesian inference and parameter uncertainty
routes.outcome: Update a prior with a likelihood to a posterior and predictive distribution for a simple return model, and explain how treating parameters as uncertain changes a decision compared with plugging in point estimates.

section_goals.goal: combine data with an economically motivated prior, compute posterior and predictive distributions, and carry parameter and model uncertainty into portfolio and model-selection decisions

routes.prerequisites: Probability and statistical inference, including likelihood.

required_readings.reason: Connect Bayesian analysis with statistical decision theory: priors, posteriors, loss and the value of information.
Survey modern Bayesian forecasting and computation to see where the specialist methods fit.

routes.checkpoint: For monthly excess returns on a market index, compute the posterior and posterior-predictive distributions of the mean under a conjugate normal model with a weak and a strong prior. Compare the predictive with the plug-in distribution, and show how the optimal mean--variance weight in the index changes with sample length and prior strength.

optional_branches.reason: Browse the Bayesian-methods-in-finance references.

routes.learning_note: Posterior updating comes before hierarchical models, shrinkage and parameter uncertainty in decisions. Frequentist covariance shrinkage is in the next section; the Bayesian interpretation of shrinkage is here.

routes.name: High-dimensional statistics and covariance estimation
routes.outcome: Explain why sample covariance matrices and many-regressor estimates fail when the number of variables is comparable with the number of observations, and name the regularisation, shrinkage or factor structure that restores stable estimates.

section_goals.goal: estimate large covariance and factor structures with explicit noise control, shrinkage and regularisation, and choose the number of factors

routes.prerequisites: Regression and time-series econometrics; eigen-decomposition.

required_readings.reason: Bridge classical inference to the bootstrap, false-discovery rates and the lasso, the tools for many simultaneous estimates.
See the lasso and its generalisations as the regression counterpart of covariance shrinkage.

routes.checkpoint: Simulate returns for 50, 200 and 500 assets with 250 observations from a known factor covariance. Compare the eigenvalues of the sample covariance with the truth and with the Marchenko--Pastur bounds, and compare the out-of-sample variance of minimum-variance portfolios built from sample, shrunk and factor covariance estimates. Fit a lasso return regression with many pure-noise predictors and report how many it selects.

optional_branches.reason: Browse the high-dimensional statistics and random-matrix references.

routes.learning_note: Covariance estimation and sampling noise come before shrinkage, regularisation and factor estimation; portfolio applications follow in Portfolio construction, estimation error and risk models ([[portfolio-construction]]).

routes.name: Numerical methods and optimisation
routes.outcome: Choose between closed-form, lattice, Monte Carlo, Fourier and PDE methods and between convex and general solvers for a stated problem, and report the numerical error and conditioning of the answer.

section_goals.goal: choose and validate numerical methods for pricing and portfolios, with error bars, sensitivities and run-time evidence

routes.prerequisites: Stochastic processes and calculus; linear algebra; programming in Python or C++.

required_readings.reason: Recognise convex problems and their duals, so that portfolio and calibration problems can be posed with certified solutions.
required_readings.selection: Duality and sensitivity analysis chapters (topic selection; numbering depends on the copy).

required_readings.reason: Learn conditioning, stability and the linear-algebra algorithms underneath every solver.

routes.checkpoint: Solve a small long-only mean--variance problem with a convex solver and report its dual variables; solve the unconstrained problem by a linear solve and report the condition number of the covariance matrix and the change in weights after a 1% perturbation of one input. Compute an implied volatility by bisection and by Newton's method and compare the iteration counts and failure cases.

optional_branches.reason: Browse the optimisation and numerical-methods references.

routes.learning_note: Numerical linear algebra and convex optimisation come before Monte Carlo, Fourier and PDE pricing; asset-specific pricing and portfolio implementations stay in their application sections.

routes.name: Asset pricing theory and empirical tests
routes.outcome: For a published return anomaly, record the claim, sample, data vintage and test, reproduce a headline estimate, and say which risk-based or mispricing explanations the evidence cannot separate.

section_goals.goal: derive the CAPM, APT and stochastic-discount-factor restrictions and confront them with the equity premium and Hansen--Jagannathan bounds
choose standard errors and weak-instrument-robust inference for financial panels and time series
estimate and test factor models and decide whether a new factor adds pricing information
judge aggregate return predictors out of sample
measure abnormal returns around events at short and long horizons

routes.prerequisites: Regression and time-series econometrics; return definitions from Financial mathematics and return measurement ([[financial-mathematics]]).

required_readings.reason: Map the field (stochastic discount factors, the CAPM and factor models, predictability and the cross-section) in one course text before the specialist pathways.
Frame return predictability and the cross-section as discount-rate variation before testing an individual factor or forecast.
Separate reproduction, extension, replication and reconciliation before relying on a published empirical result.

routes.checkpoint: Take one published return anomaly. Record the claim, sample, data vintage and test; reproduce a headline estimate from public data; then state which risk-based or mispricing explanations the evidence cannot rule out and what further test would separate them. Keep apart the question whether the variable predicts returns and the question whether a pricing model explains them.

optional_branches.reason: Browse the asset-pricing foundations section.
Go further into dynamic asset-pricing theory.

routes.learning_note: Asset-pricing theory and robust standard errors come first; factor-model tests build on both, and return predictability and event studies on the factor tests. An abnormal return measures a price effect; whether an action caused it is a question for Causal inference and experimental design ([[causal-inference]]).

routes.name: Causal inference and experimental design
routes.outcome: For a published policy or event effect, state the estimand, the identifying assumption and the main threat to it, reproduce a headline estimate, and say which confounding explanations the design cannot rule out, distinguishing the effect from a predictive or pricing relation.

section_goals.goal: choose an identification design (difference in differences, synthetic control or regression discontinuity) and test its assumptions before estimating effects
estimate heterogeneous effects and evaluate policies with causal machine learning, separating prediction from causation
design, monitor and analyse randomised, switchback and sequential experiments

routes.prerequisites: Regression and time-series econometrics; abnormal returns from Asset pricing theory and empirical tests ([[asset-pricing]]) helps for event applications.

required_readings.reason: Learn potential outcomes, assignment mechanisms and estimands such as average and local treatment effects before any design.
Use causal diagrams and target-trial reasoning to state what must be assumed for an effect to be identified.
Survey the identification strategies and robustness analyses that turn an association into a policy-relevant causal estimate.

routes.checkpoint: Take one published policy, regulatory or corporate-event effect. State the treatment, outcome, estimand and identifying assumption; reproduce a headline estimate from public data; list the confounders or spillovers the design cannot exclude and the falsification test you would run. Explain in one paragraph why a significant abnormal return or a predictive coefficient would not by itself establish the effect.

optional_branches.reason: Browse the causal-inference chapter.
Study structural causal models and the do-calculus.

routes.learning_note: Estimands and identification come first; quasi-experimental designs follow, then causal machine learning and controlled experiments, which build on them. Robust standard errors are taught in Standard errors, clustering and weak instruments ([[standard-errors-inference]]) and are not repeated here.

routes.name: Professional ethics
routes.outcome: Analyse an investment-industry conduct case by identifying the duties owed, the conflicts present and the applicable code provision or rule with its jurisdiction, and recommend an action with the disclosures and records it requires.

section_goals.goal: apply a professional code of ethics and its enforcement procedures, including market-integrity rules, to conduct cases
state the duties advisers, brokers and asset managers owe clients under US and EU rules, and manage conflicts of interest, suitability and disclosure

routes.prerequisites: No quantitative prerequisite. Familiarity with the roles of investment advisers, asset managers, brokers and analysts; Research engineering, data provenance and model validation ([[research-engineering-validation]]) helps for record-keeping.

required_readings.reason: Frame why finance needs rules and norms: without them it can become rent seeking, and public trust in it erodes.
Learn the structure of a professional code (whom it binds and its seven groups of standards) and the profession's account of ethics before the detailed guidance.
required_readings.selection: Ethics and the Investment Industry, and the Code of Ethics and Standards of Professional Conduct (front matter).

required_readings.reason: See why delegated management rests on trust, and how trust lets fees exceed costs and managers pander to client beliefs.

routes.checkpoint: Write a case memo on this scenario: an analyst at an asset manager learns of a pending block sale from a broker; the firm recommends a higher-fee in-house fund to an advisory client; and a back-test in a marketing deck omits a failed strategy. For each issue identify the duty, the CFA Institute Standard and the applicable US or EU rule with its effective date, the conflict and who is harmed, and recommend the action, disclosures and records.

optional_branches.reason: Present performance under the voluntary GIPS standards.
Browse the professional-ethics and conduct references.

routes.learning_note: Learn the code and how it is enforced first; duties to clients and conflicts under securities law build on it. Performance presentation is treated with Performance attribution and manager evaluation ([[performance-manager-evaluation]]), and client suitability is applied in Private wealth management ([[private-wealth-management]]).

routes.name: Financial statement analysis
routes.outcome: Read a listed company's annual report (statements, notes and auditor's report), reconcile net income to operating cash flow, identify the accounting policies that most affect reported profit, and state which reporting framework and standard governs each.

section_goals.goal: explain the reporting framework and the structure and articulation of the income statement, balance sheet and cash flow statement, including IFRS 18
analyse revenue, inventory, long-lived asset, lease, pension, share-based payment and income-tax accounting and its effect on comparability
consolidate groups, account for associates and joint arrangements, and translate foreign operations
compute and interpret profitability, efficiency, liquidity and solvency ratios and detect low-quality or misstated reporting
build a linked three-statement forecast with consistent balance sheets and mean-reverting profitability, and integrate the analysis

routes.prerequisites: Financial mathematics and return measurement. No accounting background is assumed.

required_readings.reason: Start from the objective of financial reporting and the elements, recognition and measurement concepts that every standard applies.
Learn how the three statements articulate under IFRS and US GAAP.
required_readings.selection: Opening chapters on the financial reporting framework and on the income statement, balance sheet and cash flow statement (topic selection).

required_readings.reason: Retrieve filings and their acceptance times from the primary source, as every later pathway does.

routes.checkpoint: Download the latest annual report of one IFRS reporter and one US GAAP reporter in the same industry. For each, reconcile net income to cash from operations, list the five accounting policies or estimates that most affect profit, and record the standard (IFRS standard or US GAAP topic) that governs each with its effective date. Note every line item whose classification differs between the two companies.

optional_branches.reason: Browse the financial-reporting and statement-analysis references.
Read accounting-based valuation alongside statement analysis.

routes.learning_note: The reporting framework and the statements come first; measurement and group reporting build on them; ratio analysis and reporting quality need measurement, and forecasting comes last. Fundamental valuation and accounting signals ([[equity-events-fundamentals]]) and Corporate credit, hybrids and labelled bonds ([[corporate-credit-capital]]) apply this section to valuation signals and creditworthiness.

routes.name: Corporate finance
routes.outcome: Explain how a company's ownership, business model and governance shape its investment, financing and payout decisions, and evaluate one decision (a project, a debt issue or a buyback) by net present value and its effect on the cost of capital.

section_goals.goal: evaluate investment projects and working-capital policy with net present value, internal rates of return and real-option logic
derive the capital-structure, cost-of-capital and payout implications of taxes, agency and asymmetric information, and test them against evidence
analyse ownership and governance, mergers and the restructuring of distressed firms

routes.prerequisites: Financial statement analysis; the CAPM from Asset-pricing theory: stochastic discount factors, CAPM and factor pricing ([[asset-pricing-theory]]) for the cost of equity.

required_readings.reason: Learn the corporate-finance framework: the firm's objective, net present value and the valuation of projects and firms.
required_readings.selection: Part 1, Introduction, and Part 3, Valuing Projects and Firms (topic selection).

required_readings.reason: Compare the theory with what chief financial officers say they do.
Learn the international benchmark for shareholder rights, boards and disclosure (2023 revision; not binding law).

routes.checkpoint: For one listed company, describe from its filings its ownership and board, business model and capital structure; then evaluate one recent decision (a project, acquisition, debt issue or buyback) by net present value at a stated cost of capital, and say which theory of capital structure or payout the decision is consistent with.

optional_branches.reason: Browse the corporate-finance, governance and restructuring references.

Then value a tranche under explicit assumptions. Take a hypothetical pool of 100 equal five-year loans with 40% recovery and the one-factor Gaussian model from [[credit-models-default]]. Compute the pool-loss distribution and the expected loss of 0--3%, 3--7% and 7--15% tranches at each annual date, for asset correlations of 10%, 30% and 50%. Do this twice. With a physical default probability from historical or hazard-model estimates, report expected tranche losses and the investor's expected return net of losses: this is loss analysis, and it is what capital and risk reduction rest on. With a risk-neutral default intensity calibrated to a stated CDS or index spread (to first order, the spread divided by one minus recovery), compute the premium and protection legs from the expected outstanding tranche notional on a stated flat discount curve, and the break-even tranche spread: this is pricing. Explain why the two expected losses differ and which one a value or spread requires. Finally, report each tranche's expected loss and value at each correlation and explain the sensitivity you find at your chosen default probability, recovery and correlations. Do not assume that the 7--15% tranche behaves like a remote senior tranche: where the expected pool loss falls inside or near a tranche, its expected loss can move in the same direction as the equity tranche's or non-monotonically as correlation rises.

Use the catalogue collectibles section for auction evidence and investable returns.

specialist_routes.name: Stablecoin pegs, runs and reserve assets
specialist_routes.parent_route: Crypto settlement, venues and derivatives
specialist_routes.outcome: Explain what holds a stablecoin at par, measure how far and why it deviates, and stress the reserve and redemption channels through which a run would spread to money markets.
specialist_routes.prerequisites: Stablecoins and tokenised bonds ([[stablecoin-tokenisation]]); currency-peg and bank-run models at the level of a money and banking course; event-study and time-series basics.

required_readings.reason: Separate demand-side arbitrage from issuance as the force that keeps Tether near par.
Treat a partly backed coin as a currency peg open to self-fulfilling attacks, and see what a dynamic conversion rule needs.
Compare collateralised and algorithmic designs and the commitment problem behind repurchase promises.
Link peg stability to the leverage demand that stablecoins finance in crypto markets.
Follow the Terra run on-chain: who left first, how fast, and through which pools.
Compare stablecoin runs with money market fund runs, including flight to safer coins and the USD 0.99 break-the-buck threshold.
Back out market-implied devaluation probabilities from Tether spot and futures prices.
Trace stablecoin flows into Treasury bill yields, and their asymmetry, as the channel to safe-asset markets.
Check a design against the international standard for legal claim, par redemption and stabilisation.
Apply settlement-finality and money-settlement principles to a coin used as a settlement asset.

specialist_routes.checkpoint: For one fiat-backed and one crypto-collateralised stablecoin, build a daily panel of secondary-market price, primary mints and redemptions, supply by chain and disclosed reserve composition. Measure peg deviations by venue and separate those that eligible arbitrageurs could close at par from those they could not. Extract a market-implied devaluation probability where futures exist, then stress a redemption wave: which reserve assets are sold first, at what haircut and how fast, and what that does to bill or deposit markets. State which reserve data are attestations rather than audits, and do not treat the peg history as evidence of resilience to a run it never faced.

optional_branches.reason: Study DAI: on-chain collateral risk, limits to arbitrage and the Peg Stability Module.
Model how the UST crash unfolded gradually before convertibility was suspended.
Reconstruct the Terra trigger events and the Anchor dependence from news and transaction data.
See how a lagged price in the minting rule broke IRON's peg in 2021.
Compare stablecoin outflows with money market fund inflows in the March 2023 banking crisis.
Test whether stablecoin volatility is statistically stable and how it responds to bitcoin.
Apply tests of absolute and relative stability to high-frequency prices.
Work through how reserve composition changes the effect of stablecoins on bank credit.
Compare with the Bank of Amsterdam, an early deposit-backed money that ended in a run.
Manage stablecoin reserves as a control problem.
Design stablecoin capital and liquidity buffers.

specialist_routes.name: Crypto leverage, liquidations and centralised lenders
specialist_routes.parent_route: Crypto settlement, venues and derivatives

specialist_routes.prerequisites: Crypto perpetuals and cross-venue basis ([[crypto-perpetuals]]); funding liquidity and margin spirals; basic order-book and event-study methods. Lending, liquidations and oracles in On-chain protocols ([[onchain-protocols]]) covers the DeFi counterpart.

See how 100x leverage was used on BitMEX, who traded it and how liquidations moved spot prices.
Measure price discovery and hedging effectiveness in BitMEX perpetual and futures contracts.
Compare perpetual and quarterly futures design and when cash-and-carry opportunities open.
Find the leveraged tether-margined perpetual as the main source of bitcoin volatility.
Rebuild funding-rate arbitrage returns with the fees, leverage and venue risk the headline backtest omits.
Formalise auto-deleveraging and its solvency, revenue and fairness trilemma, using the October 2025 cascade.
Trace the 2022 contagion from Terra through the centralised lenders and Three Arrows Capital to FTX.
Read how a centralised lender used customer coins, propped up its own token and ran short of assets.
Compare offshore margin practice with the US pilot for crypto and tokenised collateral at futures commission merchants.

specialist_routes.checkpoint: For one liquidation cascade (for example 10 October 2025), assemble open interest, funding, liquidation prints, insurance-fund balances and any auto-deleveraging notices for two venues. Write each venue's liquidation waterfall from its archived rules: maintenance margin, mark price, partial and full liquidation, insurance fund, backstop vault, then ADL ranking. Simulate a leveraged long book through the shock under both rule sets and report which positions are closed by whom at what price. Separately draw a centralised lender's balance sheet from the examiner's report and mark where customer coins were used or pledged. Label any public liquidation feed that is sampled or capped, and do not infer venue solvency from an insurance-fund balance alone.

optional_branches.reason: See spreads recover within weeks while order-book depth stays impaired after the October 2025 cascade.
Compare the FTX failure, where exchange and trading firm shared customer assets.
Contrast centralised liquidation engines with on-chain liquidation auctions and incentives.

specialist_routes.name: Crypto option markets: implied volatility, smiles and risk premia
specialist_routes.parent_route: Crypto settlement, venues and derivatives

Document the forward skew that sets bitcoin options apart from equity-index options.
Build a volatility index from thin, uneven option quotes and compare it with the VIX.
Test smile-adjusted deltas and the perpetual as the hedge instrument.
Compare delta, delta-gamma and minimum-variance hedges under jumps.
Decompose bitcoin's equity and variance risk premia by return region and volatility regime.
Measure dealers' gamma imbalance and the illiquidity premium it puts into option spreads and returns.
Read the terms of US-listed options on a spot bitcoin ETP: physical settlement, American exercise and position limits.

specialist_routes.checkpoint: At one dated snapshot, fit an arbitrage-free smile to executable Deribit bid and ask quotes for one expiry and to listed spot-bitcoin ETP options of similar tenor. Convert both to the same underlying and numeraire, reconcile forwards, and explain residual differences by settlement asset, exercise style, margin and trading hours. Compute an implied-variance index and a realised-variance series and estimate the variance risk premium with overlapping-window corrections. Then add a dealer-gamma or illiquidity measure and test whether it explains option returns out of sample. Report model fits on mid quotes as diagnostics only, and state the quote sample, filters and missing expiries.

optional_branches.reason: Estimate bitcoin pricing kernels and their U and W shapes from option-implied and physical densities.
Price options under regime switching and GARCH volatility.
Compare tree-based machine-learning pricing with Black--Scholes and Heston on crypto options.
Generate GARCH-based implied-volatility indices and a term structure.
Compare model values and Greeks with a day of early Deribit premiums.
Follow practitioner volatility commentary, noting contributor, model and observation date.

Trace what removing maker--taker fees did to market makers' spreads and customers' total costs.
Measure the return to liquidity provision across pairs and where adverse selection raises it.

Fit a square-root impact curve to reconstructed metaorders and compare it with Donier and Bonart. Reprice a passive quoting rule under the venue's fee schedule before and after one fee change, and with a 10 ms and a 100 ms latency handicap. List the edge terms you could not observe, such as queue position, hidden orders and tiered rebates.

optional_branches.reason: Profile intraday patterns in crypto volume, volatility and returns.
Compare spot and futures microstructure for bitcoin on regulated and offshore venues.

Collect normalised order-book and trade streams across exchanges for training and replay.

Check a learning market maker against the evaluation weaknesses common in the literature.

Test exogeneity, or fixed against random effects, by comparing an efficient with a consistent estimator.

specialist_routes.checkpoint: Using public firm or portfolio data, estimate a multiple regression of returns or a firm outcome on characteristics. Report OLS, White and HAC standard errors; test for heteroskedasticity, serial correlation, functional form and multicollinearity; estimate one equation by IV and by two-step GMM with an overidentifying-restrictions test; and apply a Hausman test. State which conclusion changes under each correction.

optional_branches.reason: Read regression as an approximation to the conditional expectation function, as the causal pathways do.
Read the source of the heteroskedasticity-consistent covariance matrix and its direct test.

specialist_routes.name: Stationarity, ARMA and VAR models, unit roots and cointegration
specialist_routes.parent_route: Regression and time-series econometrics
specialist_routes.outcome: Identify and estimate ARMA and VAR models, test for unit roots with the correct critical values, estimate impulse responses, test for cointegration and, only where the evidence supports it, estimate error-correction models, without falling into spurious regression or searching for a favourable test result.
specialist_routes.prerequisites: Linear regression, GMM and econometric inference.

required_readings.reason: Learn ARMA, VAR, unit roots, cointegration and state-space models.
See why the regression t statistic has a non-standard distribution under a unit root, and use Dickey--Fuller critical values.
Fit unrestricted VARs and read impulse responses instead of imposing doubtful identifying restrictions.
Specify, estimate and test multivariate VAR and cointegrated systems.
Define cointegration, move between error-correction and VAR representations, and test with the two-step residual method.
Estimate cointegrating vectors and test the cointegration rank by maximum likelihood in a VAR.

specialist_routes.checkpoint: Simulate two independent random walks and show that regressing one on the other gives a spuriously significant slope. Next, choose one related pair in advance (two share classes, a future and its underlying, or two government-bond yields), and fix the sample, deterministic terms and lag selection before looking at results. Test each series for a unit root. Only if both appear integrated of order one, run Engle--Granger and Johansen tests. If the tests support one cointegrating relation, estimate the error-correction model, the half-life of deviations and the vector error-correction model. If they do not, conclude that cointegration is not supported, model the series in levels or differences as their integration order requires, and say what this implies for a spread trade. Either conclusion completes the empirical task; do not switch to another pair to obtain a significant test. Finally, simulate a cointegrated pair with a known cointegrating vector and adjustment speed, estimate the error-correction model and the VECM, recover the half-life, and compare impulse responses from a VAR in differences with those from the VECM.

optional_branches.reason: See cointegration applied to pairs trading.

specialist_routes.name: Heavy tails, extreme values and dependence
specialist_routes.parent_route: Probability and statistical inference
specialist_routes.outcome: Test whether return tails and joint extremes are consistent with a Gaussian model, estimate tail indices, extreme quantiles and expected shortfall with extreme-value methods, and model tail dependence with copulas.
specialist_routes.prerequisites: Probability, statistical inference and resampling; maximum likelihood.

required_readings.reason: Check heavy tails, volatility clustering and leverage effects before assuming Gaussian inputs.
Estimate tail quantiles with peaks-over-threshold methods.
Model tail dependence beyond correlation.
Test whether correlation rises in bear markets once the conditioning bias of correlations measured in extremes is handled.

specialist_routes.checkpoint: For daily index and stock returns, compare Gaussian, Student-t and peaks-over-threshold estimates of 99% and 99.9% value at risk and expected shortfall; plot the mean-excess function and the tail-index estimate against the threshold and report the sensitivity. Fit Gaussian, Student-t and Clayton copulas to the joint lower tail of two equity indices and report which models the data reject.

optional_branches.reason: After Volatility forecasting, regimes and structural breaks ([[time-series-volatility]]), combine GARCH filtering with extreme-value tails.
Stress-test moment estimates under fat tails.
Browse the heavy-tails, extremes and dependence references.

specialist_routes.name: Asset-pricing theory: stochastic discount factors, CAPM and factor pricing
specialist_routes.parent_route: Asset pricing theory and empirical tests
specialist_routes.outcome: Derive the CAPM and a linear factor model from a stochastic discount factor, state the no-arbitrage conditions behind them and the APT, and test a candidate discount factor against Hansen--Jagannathan bounds and the equity premium.
specialist_routes.prerequisites: Asset pricing theory and empirical tests overview; expected utility; return measurement.

required_readings.reason: Learn the stochastic-discount-factor framework, the basic pricing equation, mean--variance frontiers and factor models, and the links between them.
required_readings.selection: Asset-pricing theory part (topic selection).

required_readings.reason: Work through single-period portfolio choice, the CAPM, the APT and consumption-based pricing in an accessible first-year PhD text.
Read the original equilibrium argument that only systematic risk is priced.
Derive approximately linear pricing from a factor structure and no arbitrage, without a market portfolio.
Connect the absence of arbitrage to the existence of an equivalent martingale measure.
Bound the volatility any admissible discount factor must have, given observed Sharpe ratios.
See why plausible consumption-based models cannot match the US equity premium and risk-free rate.

specialist_routes.checkpoint: Derive the CAPM from the pricing equation with a discount factor linear in the market return, and the beta representation of a two-factor model. Using monthly US data, compute the Hansen--Jagannathan bound from market and size or value portfolio returns and compare it with the volatility of the discount factor implied by power utility and observed consumption growth for risk aversion of 2, 10 and 50; report the risk-free rate each implies and explain the equity-premium and risk-free-rate puzzles.

optional_branches.reason: Use a rigorous treatment of portfolio choice and asset-pricing theory.
Study a graduate text unifying discount-factor and equilibrium pricing.

specialist_routes.name: Codes of ethics, professional standards and enforcement
specialist_routes.parent_route: Professional ethics
specialist_routes.outcome: Apply each group of the CFA Institute Standards of Professional Conduct (professionalism, market integrity, duties to clients and employers, investment analysis, conflicts and member responsibilities) to fact patterns, distinguish a code obligation from a legal one, and explain how a breach is investigated and sanctioned.
specialist_routes.prerequisites: Professional ethics overview.

required_readings.reason: Work through the guidance, examples and recommended procedures for Standards I--VII, including material nonpublic information and market manipulation.
required_readings.selection: Standards I--VII with their guidance and application examples.

required_readings.reason: Follow a conduct case from complaint and investigation through review or hearing panel to sanction and appeal.
Compare the code's market-integrity standard with the EU's statutory prohibitions of insider dealing, unlawful disclosure and market manipulation (applying from 3 July 2016).
Measure how common adviser misconduct is, how often it recurs and how weakly the labour market disciplines it.

specialist_routes.checkpoint: Write ten short fact patterns of your own (or adapt the handbook's scenarios without consulting their answers). For each, name the Standard engaged, decide whether there is a violation and give the procedure that would have prevented it; for the market-integrity cases, state whether the EU Market Abuse Regulation would also apply and why. Then summarise from Egan, Matvos and Seru what share of advisers have misconduct records and what happens to them, and explain what that implies for relying on enforcement alone.

optional_branches.reason: See how advisers respond to client biases in an audit study.

specialist_routes.name: Duties to clients, conflicts of interest and asset-manager responsibilities
specialist_routes.parent_route: Professional ethics
specialist_routes.outcome: State the duties of care and loyalty owed by US investment advisers, the best-interest obligation of US broker-dealers and the EU suitability requirements, apply them to a client recommendation, and design the conflict disclosures, suitability record and firm policies that the CFA Institute Asset Manager Code expects.
specialist_routes.prerequisites: Codes of ethics, professional standards and enforcement.

required_readings.reason: Learn the SEC's statement of the investment adviser's fiduciary duty of care and loyalty (United States, effective 12 July 2019).
Contrast it with the broker-dealer best-interest standard for recommendations to retail customers (United States, effective 10 September 2019).
Apply the EU guidelines on MiFID II suitability: client information, sustainability preferences, costs and switching (European Union).
Turn duties into firm policies on loyalty, investment process, trading, risk management, performance and valuation, and disclosure.
See advisers reinforce client biases that serve the adviser in an audit study (working paper).

specialist_routes.checkpoint: A retail client holds 40% of liquid wealth in an employer's stock and asks about a structured note issued by your firm. Write the recommendation file three times: as a US investment adviser, as a US broker-dealer under Regulation Best Interest, and as an EU firm under the ESMA suitability guidelines. For each, list the client information collected, the conflicts and how they are disclosed or mitigated, and the records kept. Finally, map the firm's policies to the six sections of the Asset Manager Code and identify one gap.

optional_branches.reason: See what a concentrated employer-stock holding costs an undiversified employee.

specialist_routes.name: Financial reporting frameworks and the three financial statements
specialist_routes.parent_route: Financial statement analysis
specialist_routes.outcome: Prepare and interpret a balance sheet, statement of profit or loss and cash flow statement from transactions, reconcile them through retained earnings and cash, classify cash flows under IAS 7, and apply IFRS 18's required subtotals and its disclosure of management-defined performance measures.
specialist_routes.prerequisites: Financial statement analysis overview.

required_readings.reason: Work through recognition, classification and the articulation of the three statements under IFRS and US GAAP.
required_readings.selection: Chapters on the income statement, balance sheet and cash flow statement (topic selection).

required_readings.reason: Read the presentation and cash-flow standards themselves as endorsed in the EU (regulation in force from 16 October 2023), in its current consolidated version rather than the original act.
required_readings.selection: IAS 1, IAS 7 and IAS 8.

required_readings.reason: Learn the replacement presentation standard: the operating-profit and profit-before-financing-and-income-taxes subtotals and the disclosure of management-defined performance measures (effective 1 January 2027; endorsed in the EU in 2026).
See why managers care about reported earnings and disclosure, and what they will sacrifice to meet targets.
Retrieve a company's filings and structured financial data with acceptance times.

specialist_routes.checkpoint: From a company's filed statements, rebuild the cash flow statement by the indirect method from two balance sheets and the income statement and reconcile any difference with the notes. Re-present the statement of profit or loss with IFRS 18's two new subtotals, and list any management-defined performance measure the company reports with its reconciliation to the nearest IFRS subtotal.

optional_branches.reason: Return to the Conceptual Framework when a standard is silent.

specialist_routes.name: Accounting measurement: revenue, inventories, long-lived assets, leases, employee benefits and income taxes
specialist_routes.parent_route: Financial statement analysis
specialist_routes.outcome: Explain how revenue recognition, inventory cost flows, depreciation and impairment, lease capitalisation, defined-benefit pensions, share-based payment and deferred taxes are measured under IFRS, and where US GAAP differs, and adjust two companies' statements to a comparable basis.
specialist_routes.prerequisites: Financial reporting frameworks and the three financial statements.

required_readings.reason: Learn the measurement rules and their analytical adjustments under IFRS and US GAAP.
required_readings.selection: Chapters on inventories, long-lived assets, income taxes, non-current liabilities and leases, and employee compensation (topic selection).

required_readings.reason: Check each measurement rule against the endorsed standard.
required_readings.selection: IFRS 15, IAS 2, IAS 16, IAS 36, IAS 38, IFRS 16, IAS 19, IFRS 2 and IAS 12.

required_readings.reason: See why the accrual component of earnings is less persistent than the cash component, which makes measurement choices matter for forecasts.

specialist_routes.checkpoint: For two companies in the same industry, one reporting under IFRS and one under US GAAP, restate operating profit and net debt on a common basis: align lease treatment, adjust inventory to a common cost-flow assumption where disclosed, add back impairments and separate pension service cost from financing cost. Compute the deferred-tax effect of one adjustment and report how each adjustment changes return on capital.

optional_branches.reason: Review research on accounting anomalies and fundamental analysis.

specialist_routes.name: Group accounts, intercorporate investments and foreign-currency reporting
specialist_routes.parent_route: Financial statement analysis
specialist_routes.outcome: Classify an investment as a subsidiary, joint arrangement, associate or financial asset, consolidate a group with goodwill and non-controlling interests, apply the equity method, and translate a foreign operation's statements, explaining which currency gains and losses go to profit and which to other comprehensive income.
specialist_routes.prerequisites: Financial reporting frameworks and the three financial statements; exchange-rate quotation, which Currency markets: exchange rates, premia and hedging ([[currency-markets]]) treats fully later; that section is not needed here.

required_readings.reason: Learn the classification of intercorporate investments, business combinations and the translation of multinational operations.
required_readings.selection: Chapters on intercorporate investments and multinational operations (topic selection).

required_readings.reason: Read the group, associate and foreign-currency standards as endorsed in the EU.
required_readings.selection: IFRS 3, IFRS 10, IFRS 11, IFRS 12, IAS 28, IAS 21 and IAS 29.

specialist_routes.checkpoint: Build a two-company consolidation in which a parent acquires 80% of a foreign subsidiary at a premium: record goodwill and the non-controlling interest, eliminate an intra-group sale, and translate the subsidiary's statements at closing and average rates for a currency that depreciates 15%, showing where the translation difference appears. Repeat with the subsidiary as a 30% associate under the equity method and compare reported revenue, leverage and return on equity.

specialist_routes.name: Financial ratio analysis, earnings quality and misstatement detection
specialist_routes.parent_route: Financial statement analysis
specialist_routes.outcome: Decompose return on equity into operating and financing components, benchmark ratios against their historical distribution, measure earnings quality with accrual, persistence and cash-conversion measures, and score misstatement risk.
specialist_routes.prerequisites: Accounting measurement; regression. Group accounts help for consolidated ratios.

required_readings.reason: Learn ratio families and the assessment of financial reporting quality.
required_readings.selection: Chapters on financial analysis techniques and financial reporting quality (topic selection).

required_readings.reason: Separate operating from financing activities and use ratio benchmarks for 1963--1999 to judge whether a ratio is unusual.
Choose an earnings-quality proxy knowing what it measures and what drives it.
Score the probability of a material misstatement from financial characteristics of firms subject to enforcement.

specialist_routes.checkpoint: For 20 companies in one industry over ten years, decompose return on equity into operating return, leverage and spread as Nissim and Penman do, and compare each component with their benchmark distribution. Compute total and working-capital accruals, earnings persistence and cash conversion, and estimate a misstatement score in the style of Dechow et al. Flag the three companies with the weakest reporting quality and list the note disclosures you would read next.

optional_branches.reason: Compare an earlier earnings-manipulation detection model.

specialist_routes.name: Financial statement forecasting and integrated company analysis
specialist_routes.parent_route: Financial statement analysis
specialist_routes.outcome: Build a linked three-statement forecast in which the balance sheet balances and cash flows reconcile, drive it with revenue growth, margins and asset turnover that revert to the mean at estimated rates, and test its sensitivity and consistency with valuation.
specialist_routes.prerequisites: Financial ratio analysis, earnings quality and misstatement detection; Time value of money, discounting and cash-flow valuation ([[time-value-cash-flows]]).

required_readings.reason: Forecast operating income and net operating assets from ratio drivers and link the forecasts to accounting-based valuation.
required_readings.selection: Forecasting and valuation chapters (topic selection).

required_readings.reason: Reorganise the statements into invested capital and operating profit and keep forecasts internally consistent.
required_readings.selection: Chapters on analysing and forecasting performance (topic selection).

required_readings.reason: Calibrate how fast profitability reverts to the mean, and why reversion is faster below it.
Follow a structured approach to statement modelling.
required_readings.selection: Chapter on financial statement modelling (topic selection).

specialist_routes.checkpoint: For one company, build a five-year three-statement model driven by revenue growth, operating margin, asset turnover and payout, with margin reversion calibrated to Fama and French. Check every year that assets equal liabilities plus equity and that the change in cash matches the cash flow statement; stress revenue by 10% and the margin by 2 percentage points and report free cash flow, net debt and interest cover. Close with a one-page integrated analysis that cites the measurement and reporting-quality findings of the earlier pathways.

optional_branches.reason: Connect forecasts of earnings and book value to residual-income valuation.

specialist_routes.name: Capital budgeting, project valuation and working capital
specialist_routes.parent_route: Corporate finance
specialist_routes.outcome: Value a project from incremental after-tax free cash flows at the right discount rate, compare net present value with the internal rate of return and payback, value flexibility as a real option, and set working-capital and cash policy using the cash-conversion cycle and evidence on cash holdings.
specialist_routes.prerequisites: Corporate finance overview; Time value of money, discounting and cash-flow valuation ([[time-value-cash-flows]]); Accounting measurement: revenue, inventories, long-lived assets, leases, employee benefits and income taxes ([[accounting-measurement]]) for depreciation and taxes.

required_readings.reason: Forecast incremental free cash flows, apply investment rules and manage short-term financing.
required_readings.selection: Part 3, Valuing Projects and Firms, and Part 9, Short-Term Financing (topic selection).

required_readings.reason: Revise the cash-conversion cycle, trade credit, receivables and inventory management.
required_readings.selection: Section 19.1, What Is Working Capital?, and the related working-capital sections.

required_readings.reason: Value a project with operating flexibility as a real option rather than by static net present value.
See which firms hold more cash and why: precautionary liquidity against costly external finance.

specialist_routes.checkpoint: Value a five-year expansion project from a company's filings: forecast incremental revenue, costs, capital expenditure, depreciation tax shields and working capital, discount at a stated cost of capital, and report net present value, internal rate of return, payback and the sensitivity to the discount rate. Add an option to abandon after year two and value it on a binomial tree. Then compute the company's cash-conversion cycle over five years and compare its cash holdings with the determinants in Opler et al.

specialist_routes.name: Capital structure, cost of capital and payout policy
specialist_routes.parent_route: Corporate finance
specialist_routes.outcome: Derive the Modigliani--Miller propositions and show how taxes, distress costs, agency and asymmetric information change them, estimate a company's weighted average cost of capital, and explain dividends and repurchases with irrelevance theory and the evidence on disappearing dividends.
specialist_routes.prerequisites: Capital budgeting, project valuation and working capital; Asset-pricing theory: stochastic discount factors, CAPM and factor pricing ([[asset-pricing-theory]]) for the cost of equity.

required_readings.reason: Learn the leverage-irrelevance propositions and the assumptions each needs.
Apply the same argument to dividend policy.
Add the agency costs of outside equity and debt.
See how asymmetric information makes equity issues costly and creates a financing hierarchy.
Compare the trade-off and pecking-order views of capital structure.
Value debt and choose leverage with taxes, bankruptcy costs and covenants in a structural model.
Estimate the cost of capital and value levered firms by WACC, adjusted present value and flow to equity.
required_readings.selection: Part 5, Capital Structure, and Part 6, Advanced Valuation (topic selection).

required_readings.reason: See the decline in the propensity to pay dividends and separate it from changing firm characteristics.

specialist_routes.checkpoint: Show numerically that without taxes a firm's value and weighted average cost of capital do not change as leverage rises from 0 to 60%; then add a 25% corporate tax and expected distress costs and find the value-maximising leverage. Estimate one company's cost of capital with a CAPM cost of equity, a yield-based cost of debt and market-value weights, and compare WACC and adjusted-present-value valuations. Finally, compute from public data the share of US listed firms paying dividends by year and test whether the decline survives controls for size, profitability and growth.

optional_branches.reason: Compare how practitioners say they set capital structure and the cost of capital.

specialist_routes.name: Ownership, corporate governance, mergers and restructuring
specialist_routes.parent_route: Corporate finance
specialist_routes.outcome: Explain how ownership concentration and investor protection discipline managers, evaluate a merger's motives and announcement returns, and compare out-of-court restructuring with formal bankruptcy for a distressed issuer.
specialist_routes.prerequisites: Capital structure, cost of capital and payout policy; Event studies and long-run abnormal returns ([[event-studies]]) helps for announcement returns.

required_readings.reason: Survey how legal protection of investors and large shareholders shape governance around the world.
Model governance, control rights and takeovers in one contracting framework.
required_readings.selection: Chapters on corporate governance, control rights and takeovers (topic selection).

required_readings.reason: Learn the industry clustering, payment methods and announcement returns of mergers.
See which distressed firms restructure their debt privately rather than in Chapter 11.
Follow distressed exchanges, Chapter 11 and creditor recoveries in practice.

specialist_routes.checkpoint: For one completed acquisition, compute acquirer, target and combined announcement returns with a market model, record the stated motive and the governance features (ownership, board and takeover defences) of both firms, and judge whether the deal created value. For one distressed issuer, compare each creditor class's recovery under its out-of-court exchange or Chapter 11 plan with a liquidation alternative.

optional_branches.reason: Compare a national governance code with the G20/OECD Principles.

specialist_routes.name: Household finance, human capital and lifecycle investment planning
specialist_routes.parent_route: Private wealth management
specialist_routes.outcome: Solve or simulate a lifecycle consumption and portfolio problem with labour income, labour flexibility and an uncertain lifetime, explain why the optimal equity share and annuitisation depend on human capital and longevity, and compare the result with common age-based rules.
specialist_routes.prerequisites: Private wealth management overview; dynamic programming at the level of Stochastic calculus and continuous-time control ([[stochastic-calculus-control]]).

required_readings.reason: Start from the continuous-time lifetime portfolio problem without labour income.
Add an uncertain lifetime and see why fairly priced annuities dominate bonds without a bequest motive.
Add flexible labour supply and see it raise optimal risk-taking early in life.
Solve a calibrated lifecycle model with non-tradable labour income and borrowing constraints.
Treat labour income and long horizons in strategic allocation.
required_readings.selection: Chapters on human wealth and financial wealth and on investing over the life cycle.

specialist_routes.checkpoint: Solve a discrete-time lifecycle model from age 25 to 100 with stochastic labour income, a retirement age, mortality from a published life table and constant-relative-risk-aversion utility. Report the optimal equity share by age for bond-like and for equity-like labour income, and compare welfare with a 100-minus-age rule and a target-date glide path. Then add a fairly priced life annuity at retirement and report the share of wealth annuitised and why.

optional_branches.reason: Extend the lifetime problem to optimal consumption rules.

specialist_routes.name: Taxes, asset location and concentrated positions
specialist_routes.parent_route: Private wealth management
specialist_routes.outcome: Measure after-tax returns, value the capital-gains tax-timing option and loss harvesting, locate assets across taxable and tax-deferred accounts, and design a diversification plan for a concentrated stock position that weighs tax cost against undiversified risk.
specialist_routes.prerequisites: Household finance, human capital and lifecycle investment planning; Return measurement: holding-period, time-weighted and money-weighted returns ([[return-measurement]]).

required_readings.reason: Learn the tax-timing option: realise losses and defer gains.
Quantify loss harvesting and highest-in, first-out lot selection by simulation.
Locate bonds in tax-deferred and equity in taxable accounts, and see when the rule changes.
Measure what concentrated employer stock costs an undiversified holder.
See why a single stock is more likely than not to underperform Treasury bills over its listed life.
Apply current US federal rules on basis, holding periods, capital gains and wash sales (edition for 2025 returns).

specialist_routes.checkpoint: Simulate a taxable equity portfolio over 20 years under US federal rules as stated in IRS Publication 550, with and without loss harvesting and highest-in, first-out lot selection and with the wash-sale rule enforced, and report the after-tax gain. Repeat with taxable bonds and equity split across a taxable and a tax-deferred account and check the Dammon--Spatt--Zhang location rule. Finally, for a client with 40% of liquid wealth in one low-basis stock, compare selling now, selling over five years and holding, using Meulbroek's diversification cost and Bessembinder's single-stock evidence.

specialist_routes.name: Estate planning, intergenerational transfers and family-business succession
specialist_routes.parent_route: Private wealth management
specialist_routes.outcome: Compute the transfer tax on an estate under current US federal and UK inheritance-tax rules with their effective dates, compare lifetime giving with transfers at death, and assess family against external succession for a family business on the evidence.
specialist_routes.prerequisites: Taxes, asset location and concentrated positions.

required_readings.reason: Use the US basic exclusion amount and generation-skipping transfer exemption for calendar year 2026 ($15,000,000 each).
Use the UK nil-rate band (£325,000 to 5 April 2031) and residence nil-rate band (£175,000 to 5 April 2030).
Learn the incentives for lifetime giving under US estate and gift taxes, and how little wealthy households use them.
See causal evidence that family CEO succession lowers firm performance.

specialist_routes.checkpoint: For an estate of $40 million (US) or £4 million (UK), compute the transfer tax due at death under the rules in force for 2026 (US) or the 2026--27 tax year (UK), then compare a plan of annual and lifetime gifts over ten years. State every threshold used with its source and effective date and note which are scheduled to change. For a family-owned company, set out the case for family and for external succession, citing the Bennedsen et al. estimates and their identification strategy.
